pages.title: Overview: Sanas Chrome Extension
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction The Sanas Chrome Extension is the dedicated solution for organizations running Chrome OS devices , where the Sanas Desktop Application cannot be installed. It brings Sanas Speech AI directly into the Chrome browser, enabling Chrome OS users to access Sanas. All Speech AI processing is offloaded to a remote inference backend, and the user gets access to consistent performance. Note: The Chrome Extension works only with conferencing and softphone applications that run inside a browser (for example, Zoom Web or Google Meet). Users on dedicated desktop applications must continue to use the Sanas Desktop Application instead. Refer to the comparison table to learn more. To get started, contact Sanas Support to obtain your organization's Endpoint URL . This URL is the access point that users' machines connect to for audio synthesis while using Sanas. Depending on your organization's requirements, Sanas Support will provision an Endpoint URL that points to one of the following: Option Description Sanas Cloud Sanas-hosted infrastructure, available in Singapore and the United States regions. Ideal for organizations that prefer a fully managed, low-overhead deployment. Self-Hosted Sanas Speech AI models are hosted on your organization's own infrastructure. Ideal for organizations with strict data residency or network isolation requirements. Once you have your Endpoint URL, your administrator can complete remote inference configuration in the Sanas Portal Note: Ensure that all users can reach the configured Endpoint URL from their network via HTTPS on Port 443. Extension Overview Sanas Icon The Sanas icon on the floating widget is your gateway to account-level options and resources. Click the Sanas icon to access the following: About — View extension and version information, and access the Re-personalize Voice option. Help Center — Access the Sanas Help Center for documentation and support resources. Logout — Sign out of the Sanas Chrome Extension. Controls Icon The Controls icon provides access to the main Sanas feature controls. Click the Controls icon to access the following: Sanas Toggle — Enable or disable Sanas. Voice Profile selector — Select your active voice profile for Accent Translation. Audio Device Icon The Audio Device icon provides access to your audio configuration. Available Products in the Chrome Extension The Sanas Chrome Extension currently supports the following Sanas products: Product Status Accent Translation Available Noise Cancellation Coming soon Speech Enhancement Coming soon Language Translation Coming soon Info: Support for the latest Accent Translation model will be made available in an upcoming release. Security, Privacy, and Compliance The Sanas Chrome Extension is built with a privacy-first architecture. For more information on how Sanas handles your data, refer to the following resources: Resource Description Sanas Trust Vault Security posture, certifications, and compliance documentation. Data Processing Agreement Terms governing how Sanas processes data on your behalf. Privacy Policy How Sanas collects, uses, and protects personal information. Info: The Sanas Chrome Extension follows Chrome’s standard extension update cycle . Chrome automatically checks for extension updates at regular intervals throughout the day, and most users receive updates within the same day they are released. However, the exact timing is determined by Chrome’s update process and may vary from user to user. What’s Next Quickstart Guide → Get started with the Sanas Chrome Extension. User Guide → Start using Sanas with the Sanas Chrome Extension.

pages.title: Quickstart Guide: Sanas Chrome Extension
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide walks administrators through the end-to-end setup required to deploy the Sanas Chrome Extension for their organization. By the end of this guide, the extension will be installed on a user's machine, remote inference will be configured, and ready to test their first Sanas-enabled call. Tip: For in-app guidance, search for "Configure Remote Inferencing" in the Sanas Help widget from the Sanas Portal. Before You Begin Ensure the following are in place before starting: You must have access to the Sanas Portal and have the following permissions, Group Settings or Account Settings Full Access You must have decided upon the preferred remote inferencing option — Sanas Cloud or Self-Hosted . If your organization is pursuing self-hosted inference, contact Sanas Support to complete the additional technical setup before proceeding further. You’ve understood the Chrome extension’s requirements. Refer to this decision table for help. Install the Sanas Chrome Extension Install the extension on the user's machine from the Chrome Web Store. On the user's machine, open Google Chrome Navigate to the Sanas Chrome Extension page on the Chrome Web Store. Note: The current Sanas Chrome Extension version is: 1.4.0 Click Add to Chrome On the confirmation dialog, click Add Extension The Sanas icon appears in the Chrome toolbar once the installation is complete. Note: If your organization manages Chrome browser settings centrally (for example, via Google Admin Console or a device management policy), you can push the extension to user machines without requiring manual installation. Contact Sanas Support for guidance on managed deployment. Verify Authentication Mode The Sanas Chrome Extension currently supports the following login options below. Verify that the group you are configuring uses either methods before proceeding. User Activation Key (UAK) Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Navigate to Settings > Configuration , then select Application Authentication under Platform Authentication Ensure UAK is selected. If not, update it before continuing. Single Sign-On (SSO) Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Navigate to Settings > Configuration , then select Application Authentication under Platform Authentication Ensure SSO is selected, then Domain based under redirection type. If not, update it before continuing. Note: Verify with your Sanas point of contact (POC) or contact Sanas Support to confirm that this feature has been enabled for your organization. Otherwise, it will not be accessible from your account. Configure Remote Inference on the Sanas Portal Remote inference must be configured on the Group before users can authenticate with the extension. On Portal’s Group Tree, select the Group you want to configure remote inferencing for. Note: For account-wide configuration, select your Sanas Account instead of an individual Group. Navigate to Settings > Configuration , then select Remote Inferencing under Group / Account Settings Enter the Endpoint URL provided by Sanas in the respective field, then click Save . Users will be routed to this access point while using Sanas. Note: Contact Sanas Support to obtain your Endpoint URL. Ensure that all users can reach the configured Endpoint URL from their network via HTTPS on Port 443. Once the endpoint is saved, configure the inferencing settings: On the Configuration tab, select Accent Translation under Products Select Remote Inference under Inference Mode (Optional) Select your preferred Speech AI model from the drop-down menu. Sanas automatically selects the recommended model. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle to enforce this inferencing configuration across subgroups and prevent subgroup administrators from modifying it. Click Save to apply the changes. Add Users to the Portal Add users to the Portal and assign them to the Group configured in Step 3. Refer to Add User for detailed instructions. If your organization uses the User Activation Key (UAK) authentication mode, share the following credentials with each user : Account ID — located at the top of the Group Tree. This is common across all users in your account. User ID — unique to each user. Test Your Setup Add a temporary user to the configured Group and install the Sanas Chrome Extension on your Chrome browser to verify the installation and portal configuration setup. Please refer to the next steps below on how to test the Chrome Extension. Next Steps S

pages.title: User Guide: Sanas Chrome Extension
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide walks you through accessing and using the Sanas Chrome Extension in your browser. By the end of this guide, you will be authenticated, your audio will be configured, and you will be ready to use Sanas on your next call. Before You Begin Ensure the following are in place before starting: The Sanas Chrome Extension is installed on your Chrome browser. If not, contact your administrator. Your headset is connected to your machine. Always use USB connection-based headsets for the best audio quality. You have your login credentials ready, such as Account ID and User ID for users configured on User Activation Key (UAK) , or work Email ID for users configured on Single Sign-On (SSO) . If you do not have these credentials, contact your administrator. Open the Sanas Chrome Extension Click the Sanas icon in the Chrome toolbar. This opens the Sanas floating widget on the edge of your browser window. Note: If prompted to grant microphone access, click Allow Click the Sanas icon on the floating widget to open the authentication pop-up. Authenticate If you are logging in through User Activation Key (UAK) mode, follow these steps: Enter your Account ID and User ID in their respective fields. Click Activate Key On successful authentication, the Sanas Chrome Extension interface opens. If you are authenticating through Single Sign-On (SSO) mode, follow these steps: Select SSO in the login page of the Chrome extension. Enter your work Email ID and click Continue Depending on your organization’s chosen Identity Providers (IdPs), such as Okta and Azure, your login process may require further authentication steps and proper guidance from your company IT or login admins. On successful authentication, the Sanas Chrome Extension interface opens. Configure the Extension Click the Controls icon on the Sanas floating widget. Ensure the Sanas Toggle is enabled. Verify that your preferred Voice Profile is selected — Masculine or Feminine Click the Audio Devices icon and select your connected headset from the drop-down menu. Configure Audio on Browser-based Softphones Note: We are using Google Meet web platform to demonstrate audio configuration verification in the below procedure. Configure similarly on your chosen softphone/conferencing app. For Sanas to synthesize your audio, Google Meet must route your microphone input through the Sanas audio device. As such, we preconfigured Sanas Microphone to be set by any web-based conferencing apps and softphones as their system default microphone. This allows web-based meeting applications and softphones to automatically use Sanas without requiring users to manually select it. To validate: Open Google Meet Web in your Chrome browser and sign in. Navigate to Settings > Audio, then Microphone. Sanas Microphone will show as System default Note: If a user logs out of the Sanas Chrome Extension, the Sanas Microphone remains visible in the list of available audio devices in the web app or softphone; however, Accent Translation will no longer work. Once the user signs back in, the Sanas Microphone , along with Accent Translation are automatically restored. A tab refresh may be required before they become fully functional again. Sanas is now active! Your voice will be processed through the Sanas Chrome Extension for the duration of the call. Important! Personalize your accent translated voice to sound consistently and identical. Refer Personalize voice for instructions. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Manage Groups
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview This guide provides step-by-step instructions for managing groups on the Sanas Portal. For an introduction to how groups work and best practices for structuring them, see Groups null Before you begin Ensure your Portal role includes Groups (Full Access) . Default roles like Account Admin and Group Admin have this permission. Create a Group New groups inherit configuration and product access from their parent group. Log in to the Portal In the group tree, select the parent group where you want to create the new group. Navigate to Groups & Users > Groups Click Create Group Enter the following: Group Name — A clear, descriptive name for the group. Timezone — The local timezone for this group (used for analytics and reports). Click Create Group Note: Subgroups cannot be created under the Default Group Find a Group ID Group IDs are used for bulk user imports and API integrations. In the group tree, select the parent group of the group you want to know the ID. Navigate to Groups & Users > Groups The Group ID (an 8-character alphanumeric code) is displayed in the group details. To view IDs for multiple groups, enable Include subgroups in the filter. Delete a Group Deleting a group is irreversible and only possible when the group and its subgroups (if any) have no users mapped. Move all app users out of the group (and any subgroups) before proceeding. In the group tree, select the parent group of the group you want to delete. Navigate to Groups & Users > Groups Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the group. Select Delete , then confirm your action. Note: The Default Group cannot be deleted. If deletion fails, an error message will indicate the reason. FAQ Can I move a group to a different parent? No. The hierarchy is fixed upon creation. To change a group's parent, create a new group in the correct location and move the users. What happens to reports if I change the timezone? Utilization and analytics data will be displayed according to the new timezone. Is there a limit to subgroup depth? No, but we recommend keeping your structure manageable for easier administration. Related articles Groups — Understand group hierarchy and structure. Move App Users — Clear out a group before deletion. Manage Portal Users — Assign admins to manage specific groups.

pages.title: Manage App Users
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview This guide provides step-by-step instructions for managing app users on the Sanas Portal. For an introduction to the difference between app users and Portal users, see App Users & Portal Users null Before you begin Permission: Your Portal role must include Application Users (Full Access) Target group: Identify the group where users will be added; this determines their product access and feature settings. Authentication mode: Know the authentication mode configured for the target group. See Authentication Modes Auto-Activation If the target group uses Auto-Activation , skip manual user addition. Users are automatically added to the Default Group on first login and can be moved later Add app users Log in to the Portal Select the target group in the group tree where you want to add a user. Add user Invite user Bulk add user Use this method for UAK authentication when adding users individually. Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users Click Add Users Enter the following: User ID — Enter a unique identifier (letters, numbers, and . _ + - @ only). First and Last Name (optional). To add multiple users, click Add (up to 5 per request). Click Save After adding: Share the Account ID (top of the group tree) and User ID with each user so they can sign in. Use this method for Email-Passcode authentication. Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users Click Invite Users Enter the user's work email address and hit Enter Repeat to add up to 5 email addresses per request. Click Invite App Users Sanas sends the invitation email automatically. Only work email addresses are accepted. Use this method to add a large number of users at once via CSV. Supports both UAK and Email-Passcode authentication. Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users Click Bulk Add Click Download .csv Template and save the file. Open the template and enter user details: User ID (required) — Work email for Email-Passcode, or a unique identifier for UAK. Group ID (optional) — Leave empty to add users to the current group, or specify a different Group ID Save the file and upload it to the Portal. If errors are found, download the error report, fix the issues, and re-upload. Review the action summary and confirm. Move users Move app users between groups to change their product access and configurations. Select a group in the group tree where the user is currently added. Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users. Select the checkbox next to the users you want to move. Click Move To Select the target group. Click Move To , then confirm. Users are not notified about the move. Note: We recommend moving users between groups with the same authentication mode. Moving to a group with a different mode may require re-adding the user. Edit user details You can update a user's name, but User IDs cannot be changed. To correct a User ID, deactivate the user and re-add them. Select a group in the group tree where the user is currently added. Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the user. Select Edit User Details Update the name and click Save Deactivate and Reactivate app users Deactivating a user revokes their app access immediately and releases their license seat. Note: Users cannot be permanently deleted. Deactivation preserves historical usage data for reporting and analytics. Deactivate user Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users for the user's group. Select the checkbox next to the user. Click Deactivate Users , then confirm. Reactivate user Navigate to Groups & Users > App Users for the user's group. In the status filter, select Deactivated Select the checkbox next to the user. Click Activate Users , then confirm. FAQ Are User IDs case-sensitive? No User IDs are case insensitive. User_01 and user_01 are treated as the same account. Is there a limit to how many users I can add? No limit on total users, but concurrent usage is limited by your allocated app licenses. Can I use a personal email address (e.g., Gmail)? No. Only work email domains are accepted. Why can't I delete a user? Users are deactivated rather than deleted to preserve historical usage data for reports and analytics. Related articles App Users & Portal Users — Understand the two user types. Manage Groups — Create and organize groups. Manage Portal Users — Invite and manage administrators.

pages.title: Manage Portal Users
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview This guide provides step-by-step instructions for managing Portal users (administrators) on the Sanas Portal. For an introduction to the difference between app users and Portal users, see App Users & Portal Users null Before you begin Permission: Your Portal role must include Portal Users and Access (Full Access) , or you must be an Account Admin. Scope: Portal user management is only available at the account level. Select your account at the top of the group tree. Email addresses: Have work email addresses ready for admins you want to invite. Personal email domains are not permitted. Invite Portal users Log in to the Portal Select a group in the group tree where you want to assign the user. Navigate to Groups & Users > Portal Users Click Invite Portal Users Enter work email address. Select an appropriate role from the drop-down. You can always create new custom roles for assignment. Click Send Invite to confirm. Note: If an admin hasn't accepted their invitation after a few days, click the ellipsis (⋮) next to their name and select Resend Invitation Update Portal user details You can update an admin's name, but email addresses cannot be changed. To correct an email, deactivate the admin and re-invite them with the correct address. Select your account from the group tree. Navigate to Groups & Users > Portal Users Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the admin and select Edit User Details Update the name and click Save Update the assigned role or group To change an admin's assigned role: Select the group where the admin is currently assigned. Navigate to Groups & Users > Portal Users. Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the admin and select Edit Access Select an appropriate role from the drop-down. Click Save Deactivate and Reactivate Portal users Deactivating an admin immediately revokes their Portal access. Note: Portal users cannot be permanently deleted. Deactivation preserves a log of their actions for auditing. Deactivate Select your account from the group tree. Navigate to Groups & Users > Portal Users Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the admin and select Deactivate User Click Deactivate to confirm. Note: The first Portal user (Account Admin) cannot be deactivated or reassigned. This ensures your account always has at least one Account Admin. Reactivate Reactivating restores access with the same role and group the admin had before deactivation. Select your account from the group tree. Navigate to Groups & Users > Portal Users In the status filter, select Deactivated Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the admin and select Activate User Click Activate to confirm. FAQ Can one Portal user have multiple roles? No. Only one role can be assigned per Portal user. To expand access, edit the permissions of their custom role or assign a role with broader permissions. What if an admin's email changes? Deactivate the existing admin record and invite them again with their new work email. Related articles App Users & Portal Users — Understand the two user types. Portal Roles — Learn about roles and permissions. Manage Roles and Permissions — Create and manage custom roles.

pages.title: Manage Roles and Permissions
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview This guide provides step-by-step instructions for managing custom roles in the Sanas Portal. Custom roles let you define specific permissions tailored to your organization's needs. For an introduction to roles, default permissions, and scope, see Portal Roles . To assign roles to administrators, see Manage Portal Users Before you begin Permission: You must have Account Settings (Full Access) or be an Account Admin. Scope: Role management is only available at the account level. Select your account at the top of the group tree. Create a custom role Select your account from the group tree. Navigate to Groups & Users > Role Management Click Create New Role Enter a descriptive Role Name (e.g., "Reporting Analyst" or "Regional Support Lead"). Define permissions by selecting the access level for each category: Full Access — Read and write View Only — Read only None — No access Click Create The new role is now available for assignment in Manage Access Delete a custom role You can delete custom roles that are no longer needed. The role deletion is only possible when there is no Portal user assigned to that role. Reassign any admins on the role to a different role first. See Manage Portal Users Select your account in the Group tree. Navigate to Groups & Users > Role Management Click the ellipsis (⋮) next to the custom role and select Delete Confirm the deletion. Note: Default roles cannot be deleted. Deleted custom roles are permanently removed and cannot be recovered. FAQ Can I modify or delete default roles? No. Default roles (Account Admin and Group Admin) are system-generated and cannot be changed or deleted. What happens when I update a custom role's permissions? All admins assigned to that role immediately receive the updated permissions. Can one admin have multiple roles? No. Each admin is assigned a single role. If broader access is needed, create a custom role with the combined permissions. Related articles Portal Roles — Understand roles, permissions, and scope. Manage Portal Users — Assign roles and manage administrators. Manage Groups — Create and organize groups.

pages.title: On-Demand AI-model Update
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction On-demand AI model update lets you deploy specific AI models for Accent Translation, Speech Enhancement, and Noise Cancellation at the group level, directly from the Sanas Portal. Updates download in the background and apply automatically; agents stay on their calls without interruption. AI model updates are independent of the app release cycle. You never need to push an app reinstall for a model change. Feature overview Available On Accent Translation, Noise Cancellation, and Speech Enhancement Supported Sanas App Version V5.2.x and above Required Permissions Group settings : Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings : Full access ( to configure account-wide) How it works You can trigger an AI model update in two ways: Automatic update: Sanas recommends and deploys the optimal model when you change accent configurations (for the Sanas AT product). Manual update: You select a specific model version for any supported product. User experience during an AI model update What agents experience depends on whether the target accent changes. Target accent changes (for example, US → UK) AT pauses until the new AI model finishes downloading. During this time, Noise Cancellation remains active, and calls continue without interruption. Once the download completes, AT resumes automatically with the updated AI model. Tip Give your team a heads-up before switching target accents during active call hours. No target accent change When the target accent stays the same — for example, you're updating the model version, agents don't notice anything. AT and NC continue running on the current model while the new model downloads in the background. Once ready, the app switches to the new model on the next routine sync. For admins: Configure AI models Automatic AI model update Use this method when you're configuring or changing accents for the Accent Translation product. Sanas recommends the optimal model automatically. Sign in to the Portal and select the target group from the Group Tree. Verify that the group has access to the AT product. Navigate to Settings Configuration , then select Accent Translation under Products Configure the source and target accents based on your team's requirements. Review the pre-selected recommended AI model, then select Save to deploy. Note Agents continue using Noise Cancellation while the new AT model downloads. AT becomes available again once the download completes. Manual AI model update Use this method when you want to select a specific model version for any supported product — Accent Translation, Speech Enhancement, or Noise Cancellation. Common scenarios include Piloting early-access models: Test a new AI model release on a small group before rolling it out broadly. Optimizing for hardware constraints: Deploy a lighter model for agents on lower-spec machines. Steps: (Optional) To access early-release models, enable Experimental Features under Settings Configuration Experimental Features Navigate to Settings Configuration , then select the product you want to update ( Accent Translation Speech Enhancement , or Noise Cancellation ). Select your preferred AI model from the dropdown. Select Save to deploy. The model downloads to agent devices based on the group's configured Download Preferences FAQ Do users need to restart their computer for the new model to take effect? No. The model is applied automatically once the download completes. It loads on the next routine app sync. What happens if the download is interrupted by a poor internet connection? Sanas manages downloads resiliently. If the connection is lost, the download pauses and resumes automatically once the agent is back online. Can I revert to an older AI model? Yes. Use the manual update method to select a previous model version and save the configuration. Related articles Authentication Modes Manage how users verify their access. Automatic volume optimization Set up a smooth calling experience for your team. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Sanas Personalization
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Your voice is a key part of your identity. With Sanas Personalization, you don't have to choose between clarity and character. This feature ensures your accent-translated voice sounds close to your natural voice by preserving traits like pitch, amplitude, and speech patterns, while keeping the output accent-neutral and easy for recipients to understand. Once a voice profile is created, the same personalized voice is applied across all calls and devices, giving the Sanas App and Chrome Extension users consistent, authentic identity without compromising accent translation quality. Feature overview Available On Accent Translation Supported Sanas App Version V5: 5.2.x and above Supported Sanas Chrome Extension Version V1.3.2 and above Required Permissions Group settings: Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings: Full access (to configure account-wide) How it works Voice Personalization involves a one-time setup: Enablement: An admin enables the feature for a group in the Portal. Notification: Eligible users receive a prompt in their Sanas App to begin setup. Profile creation: The user completes a short voice reading (less than 60 seconds). Deployment: Sanas analyzes the input and automatically assigns the best-matched voice profile. Monitoring: Admins track personalization status for their team in the Portal. For Portal Admin: Enable and monitor Voice Personalization Enable Voice Personalization Sign in to the Portal and select the desired group from the Group Tree. Navigate to Settings Configuration Under Desktop Application , locate Application Settings Locate Sanas Personalization and toggle it on. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle to prevent subgroups from overriding this setting. Reviewing adoption status To check personalization status for individual users: Select the desired group from the Group Tree. Navigate to Groups & User > App Users Review the Personalize column to identify personalization status for each user and the timestamp of their personalization. For App User: Creating Your Voice Profile Initial Setup Launch your Sanas app and authenticate, if required. A pop-up for Sanas Personalization will appear. Connect a high-quality headset, and ensure it is selected. Click Start Read the script at your natural pace. When you're done, select Stop Select Continue to Sanas to activate your personalized voice. Note: If profile creation fails or you're not satisfied, select Try Again to re-record. Your new personalized voice is now active. Re-profile your voice If you need to recreate your profile — for example, if you recorded in a noisy environment or changed your headset: Open the Sanas App and authenticate, if required. Navigate to More About Select Re-personalize Voice For Chrome Extension User Before You Begin Ensure the Sanas Personalization feature is enabled for the intended Group from the Portal. Refer to Enable Sanas Personalization for instructions. Personalize Your Voice On your first login, a Sanas Personalization pop-up appears automatically in your browser window. Note: Ensure your headset is connected before beginning personalization. On the Sanas Personalization pop-up, click Personalize On the script prompt window, ensure your connected headset is selected, then click Start Read the displayed script aloud at your natural pace. Once done, click Stop Your voice profile is saved and will be applied automatically to future sessions. Re-Personalize Your Voice If you are not satisfied with your current voice profile, you can re-personalize it at any time. Click the Sanas icon on the floating widget. Click About , then click Re-personalize Voice On the script prompt window, ensure your connected headset is selected, then click Start Read the displayed script aloud at your natural pace. Once done, click Stop Your voice profile is updated immediately. FAQ Do I need to create a voice profile every time I log in to a different device? No. Your voice profile is linked to your user ID. Once you create it, it follows you to any device where you sign in with your Sanas credentials. Does Sanas store my voice recordings? No. Sanas does not store your audio recordings. The audio is only used during the short profiling session to assign the most appropriate voice profile to your user ID. Does the personalized voice affect the clarity of accent translation? No. Voice Personalization adjusts the tone and characteristics of your voice. The AI continues to ens

pages.title: Omnidirectional Noise Cancellation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Omnidirectional Noise Cancellation removes background noise from both sides of a call — yours and your recipient's — giving you a completely noise-free calling experience. All processing happens on your device; your recipients don't need to install anything. Feature Overview Available On Noise Cancellation Supported Sanas App Version 5.2.x and above. Required Permissions Group settings: Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings: Full access (to configure account-wide) How it works Omnidirectional NC works in the following stages: Enablement : As an admin, enable the Omnidirectional NC feature for a group having access to the Noise Cancellation feature. App user usage : Once enabled, the intended Sanas app users start seeing two dedicated toggles for Noise cancellation. The update should happen on their next automatic app sync. For admins: Enable Omnidirectional NC Log in to the Portal and select the intended group from the Group Tree. Navigate to Settings Configuration Under Products , select Noise Cancellation Enable the Inbound Noise Cancellation toggle. (Optional) Enable the Toggle-ability feature to prevent users from manually disabling NC controls from the Sanas App. (Optional) Enable Lock Configuration to prevent subgroup admins from overriding this setting. For users: Audio routing setup For Sanas to process audio from both sides of the call, your audio devices must be routed correctly in two places. 1. Configure the Sanas App In the Sanas App, select your physical hardware: Input Device: Your headset microphone. Output Device: Your headset earphones. 2. Configure your communication platform In your softphone or conferencing software (Zoom, Teams, dialers), select the following Sanas audio devices: Platform Input Device Output Device Windows Sanas Audio Sanas Audio macOS Sanas Microphone Sanas Speaker Important: Sanas needs constant access to your audio stream to perform synthesis. To do that, configure your softphone’s audio sources (input and ouput audio) to above Sanas devices based on your used platform. And that’s it, now you can independently control the NC toggle in the Sanas App during your calls. FAQ Does this work if my recipient is in a very noisy environment, like a street or a busy office? Yes. The AI model isolates the recipient's voice from the incoming audio stream and suppresses background noise, regardless of the caller's environment. Will this affect my computer's performance? Sanas is optimized for enterprise hardware. Processing both audio streams has minimal impact on system performance. Can I turn off just the incoming noise cancellation? Yes. Disable the NC toggle for incoming audio in the Sanas App. Related articles Automatic Volume Optimization Keep your audio levels consistent in real time. Toggle-ability Guide Learn how to enforce specific app settings for your team. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Automatic Volume Optimization
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Automatic Volume Optimization (AVO) dynamically adjusts audio levels in real-time, preventing speech from being too quiet or distortedly loud. It maintains a steady output throughout every call. Feature overview Available on All Sanas products ( Noise Cancellation Accent Translation Speech Enhancement , and Language Translation Supported Sanas App version v5.2.x and above Required Permissions Group settings: Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings: Full access (to configure account-wide) How it works AVO processes outgoing audio in real time, normalizing volume levels before the audio reaches your recipient. It works independently of Noise Cancellation and does not require any calibration or setup from users. Once enabled by an admin, AVO activates automatically on the user's next app sync with the Portal. For admins: Enable AVO To deploy AVO, simply enable it in the group configurations. You can target specific groups or enable it at the Account Level for your entire organization. Prerequisites Environment setup: Disable any built-in audio or voice enhancement features in your conferencing software (Zoom, Teams, or dialers) to avoid interference with AVO. Enable AVO for a group Sign in to the Portal and select the intended group from the Group Tree, or select the account for organization-wide configuration. Navigate to Settings Configuration Under Desktop Application , locate Application Settings Enable the Automatic Volume Optimization toggle. (Optional) Enable Lock Configuration to prevent subgroup admins from overriding this setting. Note: Once enabled, AVO start working from the next auto app sync. App users can not disable AVO from their Sanas app. FAQ Do users need to perform a voice calibration for AVO? No. AVO works from the start of a call with no user calibration required. How can I verify that AVO is working for my agents? Perform a test call with users before their calling session to verify consistent audio levels. Will AVO accidentally amplify background noise? No. AVO operates independently of Noise Cancellation or Speech Enhancement. It focuses only on normalizing speech volume. Related Articles Sanas Personalization Carry your unique identity through your accent-translated voice. On-Demand Model Update Control your team's deployed AI model remotely. Authentication Modes Manage how your users log in to the Sanas app. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Toggle-Ability for User Preference
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Toggle-ability controls whether users can manually enable or disable controls from the Sanas desktop app. When Toggle-ability is enabled (the default), users have full control over their product toggles. When an admin disables Toggle-ability, the toggles in the Sanas App lock in the enabled position, and users can no longer turn products off. By default, this feature is enabled , granting users full control. When Disabled by an administrator, the user’s ability to toggle settings is revoked, enforcing the organization's required configuration. Feature overview Available On All Sanas products (Noise Cancellation, Accent Translation, Speech Enhancement, and Language Translation) Supported Sanas App Version Group settings: Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings: Full access (to configure account-wide) Required Permissions Group settings: Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings: Full access (to configure account-wide) How Toggle-ability works State What happens Enabled (default) App users have full control. They can control Sanas products in the app as required. Disabled Product toggles in the Sanas App lock in the Enabled position. Users cannot disable the controls in the app. Sync behavior: If a user currently has Sanas disabled and an admin disables Toggle-ability for their group, the app automatically switches Sanas to enabled and locks for the user on the next app sync. Note: Disabling Toggle-ability also disables controls from the Sanas widget for the impacted users. For admins: Configure Toggle-ability Disable Toggle-ability for a group Sign in to the Portal and select the intended group from the Group Tree, or select the account for organization-wide configuration. Navigate to Settings Configuration Under Desktop Application , locate Application Settings Turn off the Toggle-ability toggle. Select Save (Optional) Enable Lock Configuration to prevent subgroup admins from overriding this setting. Tip Decide whether to apply this at the account level or target specific high-priority groups first. You can always expand later. FAQ Can a user bypass the user preference by restarting their computer? No. The Toggle-Ability configuration is tied to the user's account in the Portal. As soon as the app launches and syncs, the user preference will be reapplied. Does Toggle-Ability affect the Sanas Widget? Yes. If Toggle-Ability is disabled, the App user can no longer disable Sanas from the widget as well. Related Articles Sanas Widget Guide Quick-toggle overlay for Accent Translation controls. Manage App Users Override settings for individual agents or groups. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Sanas Widget
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introuction The Sanas Widget is a compact overlay that gives you quick access to Sanas controls without switching back to the full app. When you minimize the Sanas App, the Widget stays on top of your screen — whether you're on a local computer or a virtual desktop. The Widget also provides real-time visual feedback so you can confirm Sanas status at a glance. Feature overview Available on All Sanas products (AT, SE, NC, and LT). Supported Sanas App Version V5.2.x and above Required permissions Group settings: Full access (to configure for a group) Account settings: Full access (to configure account-wide) For Admin: Enable the Widget for a group Sign in to the Portal and select the intended group from the Group Tree, or select the account for organization-wide configuration. Navigate to Settings Configuration Under Desktop Application , locate Application Settings Enable the Sanas Widget toggle. (Optional) Enable Lock Configuration to prevent subgroup admins from overriding this setting. The Widget becomes available to users on their next app sync with the Portal. For users: Using the Sanas Widget Access the Widget Minimize the Sanas App. The Widget appears as a small overlay on your screen. You can drag it to any position that doesn't interfere with your softphone or other running applications. Sanas Widget toggle The Sanas Widget toggle helps you take the following quick actions based on the Sanas product you're currently using: Accent Translation — Enable/Disable Accent Translation. Noise Cancellation (outbound and inbound) continues running until disabled separately from the Sanas full app. Speech Enhancement — Enable/Disable outbound Speech Enhancement. Inbound Speech Enhancement continues running until disabled separately from the Sanas full app. Noise Cancellation — Enable/Disable outbound Noise Cancellation. Inbound Noise Cancellation continues running until disabled separately from the Sanas full app. Language Translation — Enable/Disable Language Translation. Visual feedback The Widget provides two types of real-time status indicators: Audio waveform animation When the Widget is visible, and Accent Translation is enabled, an audio waveform animation indicates that Sanas is actively processing your audio. Taskbar color indicators The Sanas icon in your taskbar reflects the current status: Color Meaning Red Sanas is disabled. Amber Sanas is enabled, but audio is not synthesizing. The reason could be a misconfigured audio source in the softphone. Green Sanas is actively synthesizing audio. Tip: If you see a red indicator during a call, check that your softphone's input and output devices are set to the Sanas audio devices and Sanas is enabled from the app. FAQ Does the Widget work on virtual desktops? Yes. The Widget overlays on both local and virtual desktop environments. Can I reposition the Widget on my screen? Yes. Drag the Widget to any location on your screen. Do I need the Widget to use Sanas? No. The Widget is a convenience feature. You can always use the full Sanas App to control Accent Translation. The Widget isn't appearing when I minimize the app. What should I do? Confirm that your admin has enabled the Widget for your group, and that you're running Sanas App V5.2.x or higher. If both are correct, re-initiate your Sanas app session for instant syncing. Related articles Sanas App User Guide Full guide to using the Sanas desktop application. Omnidirectional Noise Cancellation Remove background noise from both sides of a call. Sanas Personalization Carry your unique identity through your accent-translated voice. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Create Custom Glossary for Language Translation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Configure a custom glossary to prevent specific terms from being translated during multilingual calls. This is useful for industry-specific terminology, brand names, product names, or technical words that should be spoken as-is in the original language. A custom glossary is available for Language Translation and can be configured at the Group or Account level. Configuring at the Account level applies the glossary settings across all groups, while group-level configuration lets you tailor the glossary for specific teams. How it works When a user speaks a term that exists in the custom glossary during a call, Sanas detects the term automatically and preserves it in the original language instead of translating it. This ensures that critical terminology is not misinterpreted or altered during translation. Custom glossary has two separate Lock Configuration toggles, each with a different scope: Feature lock — Ensures all subgroups have the Custom Glossary feature enabled. Subgroups cannot disable it, but they can still define and maintain their own glossary terms. Glossary lock — Ensures all subgroups use the same glossary terms as the parent group. Subgroups cannot modify existing glossary terms. See Lock Configuration to learn more. Before you begin Ensure your Portal role has Group Settings: Full access Ensure the group has access to Language Translation. You can verify this under Settings > Feature Management Create a custom glossary Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Select a group on the Group Tree for which you want to configure the glossary. Alternatively, select Account to apply a common glossary across all groups. Groups can override these settings unless Lock Configuration is enabled. Navigate to Settings > Configuration > Language Translation Note: If Language Translation isn't listed under products, verify the group's feature access under Settings > Feature Management. Enable the Use Custom Glossary toggle. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle for the feature to ensure all subgroups have Custom Glossary enabled. Add terms to the glossary: Enter the words or phrases you want to add, then press Enter Return . Repeat for all terms you want to include. Note: Consider adding industry-specific terminology or product names that should remain untranslated, such as drug names, brand names, or proprietary terms. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle for the glossary to ensure subgroups use the same glossary terms as this group. Click Save to apply the changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure Languages for a Group
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Language Translation processes speech using the source and target languages configured for each Group. These settings take effect as defaults for all Sanas App users in the group upon app activation. Sanas translates between the configured languages bidirectionally, enabling real-time multilingual conversations between your agents and their recipients. Configure languages at the Account level to apply a common baseline language across all groups, or at the group level to tailor settings for specific teams. Language types Configure the following language types: Source language — The language the Sanas App user speaks. This is the input language Sanas uses for translation. Target language — The language the call recipient speaks. Set this based on the primary preferred language of the recipients your team interacts with. Info: Configuring languages at the Account level applies a common baseline across all groups. Group-level configuration lets you tailor language settings for specific teams. Language configuration locks Language configuration has two independent Lock Configuration toggles, one for each language type: Source language lock — Ensures all subgroups use the common source language. Target language lock — Ensures all subgroups use the common target language. These locks can be enabled independently, giving you flexibility to enforce one language while allowing users to modify the other. See Lock Configuration to learn more. Note: Once a language lock is configured: App user can not modify the selction from the Sanas App. Subgroup admin cannot modify the language selection from the Portal. Before you begin Ensure your Portal role has Group or Account Settings: Full access Ensure the group has access to the Language Translation product. You can verify this under Settings > Feature Management Configure languages Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Select a group on the Group Tree for which you want to configure the languages. Alternatively, select Account to apply common language settings across all groups. Groups can still override these configurations unless Lock Configuration is enabled. Navigate to Settings > Configuration > Language Translation Select the Source and Target languages from their respective drop-down menus. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle if required. You can enable the locks independently for each language type. Click Save to apply the changes. Note: The updated langauge configurations gets applied to users on the next app sync. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Automatic Deactivation of Inactive App Users
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Managing user licenses efficiently ensures that Sanas App access is not held by inactive users, keeping your license pool available for active team members. Manually tracking inactivity across a large user base is time-consuming. The Inactive App Users feature in the Sanas Portal automates this process. You can configure it to automatically deactivate users who exceed a defined inactivity period, freeing up licenses without manual intervention. Note: Deactivated users can be reactivated at any time from the Portal to restore their Sanas App access. How is app user inactivity calculated? A user is considered inactive when no app activation (app log in) is detected within 24 hours. The inactivity period is computed per the UST timezone. Example: A group has the Inactive App Users feature configured with a 15-day inactivity period: User A goes on a week-long vacation. Inactivity tracking begins on Day 1. Because they return and activate the app on Day 8, they are still within the inactivity period and retain access without interruption. User B is moved to a project that does not use the Sanas App. After 15 days without activating the app, their status is updated to Deactivated in the Portal. User B must contact their admin or supervisor to be reactivated before they can log in again. Before you begin Ensure your Portal role has Account Settings: Full Access to complete this configuration. Configure Inactive App Users Log in to the Portal using your credentials. Select your Sanas Account on the Group Tree. Note: Inactive users deactivation can be configured at account level only. Navigate to Settings Configuration Inactive App Users Enable the Deactivate Inactive App Users toggle. From the Deactivate after dropdown, select the number of days after which inactive users are automatically deactivated. The default is 30 days Click Save to apply the changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Auto Enable Sanas on App Launch
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Auto Enable Sanas automatically enables Sanas at the beginning of each new app session, ensuring users do not need to manually toggle Sanas On before a call. When the feature is configured, Sanas toggles get enabled for both incoming and outgoing audio across Accent Translation Noise Cancellation , and Speech Enhancement The auto enable works when the app user launches and authenticates on the Sanas App. Before You Begin Ensure your Portal role has Group or Account Settings: Full Access permissions to configure this feature. Configure Auto Enable Sanas Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. On the Group Tree , select the Group you want to configure. To apply this configuration across all Groups, select your Sanas Account instead. Navigate to Settings Configuration Application Settings Enable the toggle next to Auto Enable Sanas on App Launch (Option) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle to prevent subgroup admins from modifying this setting. Click Save . Auto Enable Sanas is now active for all App Users in the selected Group. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure Lock Voice Profile Selection
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Voice profiles determine the characteristics of a user's accent-translated speech on the Sanas App. Users select a voice profile — Masculine or Feminine — to help Sanas assign the closest-matching translated voice. Lock Voice Profile is an admin-controlled feature on the Sanas Portal that enforces a voice profile for users within a Group or Account. Once enabled, the selected voice profile is locked on the Sanas App and cannot be modified by the user. Admins retain the ability to review and update individual users' locked voice profiles directly from the Portal. How It Works Lock Voice Profile follows a three-stage workflow: Admin configuration — An admin enables Lock Voice Profile for a Group or Account from the Sanas Portal. User profile selection — Users who have never selected a voice profile receive a prompt on the Sanas App to select a voice profile (Masculine or Feminine). Users who have previously configured a voice profile have their existing selection locked automatically. Admin review and modification — Admins can review each user's locked voice profile in the App Users table and update it directly from the Portal if required. Before You Begin Ensure your Portal role has Group or Account Settings: Full Access permissions to configure this feature. Configure Lock Voice Profile Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Select a Group on the Group Tree you want to configure. Select your Sanas Account to configure the feature account-wide instead. Navigate to Settings Configuration Accent Translation Scroll down to locate Lock Voice Profile and enable the toggle. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle to prevent subgroup admins from modifying this setting. Click Save. Review/modify User Voice Profile Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. On the Group Tree , select the Group the user belongs to. Navigate to Groups & Users App Users In the App Users table, review the voice profile status against each user: Note: A “ in the Voice Profile column indicates that the user has not yet made a voice profile selection. To update a user's voice profile: Click the ellipsis ( ) next to the user, then select Change Voice Profile Select a voice profile from the drop-down, then click Save Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure Speech Enhancement Modes
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Sanas Speech Enhancement SE ) features built-in enhancement modes that enable you to optimize audio performance in various use-case scenarios. This article describes each mode and explains how to configure them. Enhancement Modes Standard A multi-speaker mode that preserves background human speech while canceling environmental noises. Recommended for shared workstations and open-desk setups. Voice Isolation A single-speaker mode that preserves only the primary speaker's voice while canceling distant human speech and environmental noise. Recommended for agents using a headset or personal microphone. Voice Isolation includes the following sub-modes: Sub-mode Description Best for Auto Automatically detects the headset type. When app users are using various headset types Headset mic Detects primary speech in the near field. Agents using headsets with a boom microphone. Built-in mic Detects primary speech in the far field. Agents using a laptop's built-in microphone or headsets without a boom microphone. Note: Standard is the default enhancement mode for SE. Before you begin Ensure your Portal role has Group or Account Settings: Full Access permissions to modify the configuration. Configure the enhancement mode Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. On the Group Tree , select the Group you want to configure. To apply the configuration across all Groups, select your Sanas Account instead. Navigate to Settings Configuration Speech Enhancement Select an enhancement mode: Standard — For multi-speaker environments. Voice Isolation — For single-speaker environments. Select the appropriate sub-mode based on the agent's microphone setup: Auto — Headset type is detected automatically. Headset mic — Agent uses a headset with a boom microphone. Built-in mic — Agent uses a laptop's built-in microphone or headset without a boom microphone. Select your preferred Speech AI model from the respective drop-down menu of your selected enhanced mode. Sanas selects the recommended model automatically. Click Save . The updated mode applies to all agents in the selected Group. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Schedule Sanas Reports
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Create schedules to have Sanas Reports delivered automatically to admins or managers at a defined frequency. Scheduled reports eliminate the need to manually export reports from the Portal; recipients receive them directly by email. Note: There is no limit on the number of scheduled reports you can create. Create a schedule Log in to the Portal using your credentials. On the Group Tree , select the Group you want to configure. Navigate to the Reports page. Click Get Reports , then click Schedule Click Create New Schedule and fill in the following details: Reports: Select the checkbox next to each report you want to include. Name: Enter a descriptive name for the schedule. Duration: Select the app utilization period to include in the reports: Last 30 days Month to Date Week to Date Cadence: Select how frequently the report should be delivered: Daily Weekly Monthly Note: For each cadence option, configure the time, date, or day of delivery. Time is in UTC Send to: Enter the email addresses of the recipients. Click Schedule View or update a schedule Log in to the Portal and navigate to Reports Get Reports Schedule Click View All Schedules to see all previously created schedules. Click the ( ) ellipsis next to the schedule you want to update, then click Edit Schedule Update the schedule as required. Click Schedule to apply the changes. Delete a schedule Log in to the Portal and navigate to Reports Get Reports Schedule Click View All Schedules. Click the ( ) ellipsis next to the schedule you want to update, then click Delete Schedule Click Remove to confirm. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Overview: Sanas Application
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction The Sanas Desktop Application ( Sanas App ) is your platform for accessing Sanas products; the AI-powered tools that help you sound clear, confident, and understood on every call. The app runs quietly in the background while you focus on your conversations, with app controls that stay within your reach at all times. This guide walks you through the app's interface, controls, and key features so you know exactly what everything does before you start using it. User workflow Getting started with the Sanas App follows three steps: Authenticate —Sign in to the Sanas app using your credentials. Set your controls — Navigate to your Sanas product and enable the necessary controls. Verify your audio — Confirm that your softphone or conferencing platform is using the correct audio configuration before you start taking calls. For detailed instructions, see the Sanas App user guide Product tabs A vertical tab layout on the left side of the app lets you navigate between your available Sanas products. The currently selected product is visually highlighted. Note: Your access to Sanas products is managed by your administrator. If you don't see a product you expect, reach out to your admin. App controls Use the primary controls on the app to manage your Sanas product usage. Each product has its own set of controls, described in the sections below. Imporant to know before you start: Admin reporting : Every time you disable an app control toggle, the action is logged in your administrator's activity log. Your administrator can see when controls were turned off and for how long. Locked controls : Your administrator can lock toggle responsiveness. When this is active, you cannot manually change app controls, the app runs with your administrator's preconfigured preferences. If your toggles appear unresponsive, this is likely the reason. Accent Translation Noise Cancellation Language Translation Speech Enhancement Accent Translation AT ) adjusts your accent in real-time so your recipients can understand you more easily without altering your voice identity. Use AT if your role involves speaking with customers in a different region or accent group. Accent Translation (AT): Toggle AT on or off during your calls. When AT is enabled, select a voice type between Masculine or Feminine to match your natural voice. Noise Cancellation (NC): Manage NC independently for outgoing audio (what you say) and incoming audio (what you hear) using dedicated toggles. Use both toggles when you're in a noisy environment; use just the incoming toggle if your recipient's background is noisy, but yours is quiet. Fallback NC: When you disable the AT toggle, the app automatically switches to NC-only mode. This is by design to ensure your call remains noise-free even when you have disabled AT. To stop NC as well, disable the NC toggles separately. Noise Cancellation NC ) removes background noise from your calls in real-time. Use NC when you're working in a shared or noisy space, or when your customer's environment is making it hard to hear them clearly. What you say (outgoing audio): Controls NC on your voice, so your recipient hears clean audio free of your background noise. What you hear (incoming audio): Controls NC on your recipient's voice, so you hear them clearly regardless of their environment. Language Translation LT ) translates your conversation in real-time, allowing you to have bi-directional multilingual conversations with your customers. Use LT when you're handling calls with customers who speak a different language. Language Translation (LT) : Toggle LT on or off during your calls. When LT is enabled, and language preferences are configured, your speech is translated in real time into your recipient's preferred language, and your recipient's speech is translated back into yours. I Speak: Select the language you speak. This sets the input language for translation. They Speak: Select the language your recipient speaks. Your voice is translated into this language for your recipient. Transcription: Enable the transcription toggles to get a real-time text transcript of your conversation — useful for reviewing details after a call or following along during complex interactions. Speech Enhancement SE ) provides high-fidelity, crystal-clear calls in real-time. Use SE when you're working in a shared or noisy space, or when your customer's environment is making it hard to hear them clearly. What you say (outgoing audio): Controls S

pages.text: summary Prev Next This guide helps you get started with the Sanas Desktop Application. You'll learn how to sign in, configure the app, and verify your audio setup before you make your first call. Using Sanas for the first time? Take the app tour to explore the app controls and menu options before you begin. Before you begin Complete these preparation steps to ensure a smooth setup: App installation : The Sanas App is installed on your computer. If you don't see it, contact your administrator for installation. Authentication credentials : You have your app authentication credentials — User ID and Account ID , if provided by your administrator. If you haven't received credentials, your account may be configured for a different authentication mode. Try the available options in Step 1 before reaching out to your administrator. Headset : A USB-based headset is connected to your computer. USB headsets work best with Sanas and provide the best audio quality. Who should use this guide? What will you accomplish? This guide is for Sanas App users who have been granted access by their administrator. By the end of this guide, you'll: - Sign in to the Sanas App. - Configure your assigned Sanas products. - Verify audio device settings on your softphone. - Estimated time: 15 minutes. Step 1: Sign in to the Sanas application Launch the Sanas App on your computer. You're signed in to your computer using your user profile. Your computer is connected to your organization’s hostname. You're signed in to your computer using your user profile. No action required. The app authenticates automatically when you launch it. Troubleshooting: If Auto Activation fails, confirm both requirements above are met, then relaunch the app to retry. Enter your work email address. Select Sign in Enter the verification code sent to your email. Select the SSO option shown in the app. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete authentication. Note: If you can't find the right authentication option or experience issues signing in, contact your administrator. Step 2: Configure your Sanas product Now that you're signed in, configure the app based on the products your administrator has enabled for your account. Select your product below: Note: Avoid using built-in laptop microphones or webcam microphones. Always use a USB-based headset for best results. Audio sources (applies to all products) Before configuring product-specific controls, set your audio sources. This setting is shared across all Sanas products — you only need to do this once. Device Setting Microphone Select the microphone of your connected USB headset. Speaker Select your connected USB headset. Sanas product Now, configure the controls for the Sanas product you want to use as described below: Accent Translation Noise Cancellation Language Translation Speech Enhancement App controls Keep the Accent Translation (AT) toggle to utilize AT during your calls. By default, the Noise Cancellation toggles are also enabled and require a separate action to disable after AT is turned off. pages.title: Best Practices for Sanas App Users
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Getting the most out of Sanas comes down to a few key habits, how you wear your headset, how you speak, and how you maintain your setup. This guide covers the essentials so you can deliver clear, natural audio on every call, regardless of which Sanas product you're using. Microphone positioning Your headset’s position is a critical factor affecting the overall audio quality. Poor positioning may cause Sanas to miss certain parts of your speech, especially in scenarios where your pitch or volume fluctuates mid-sentence. 1. Adjust your headset for a comfortable fit Adjust the headband length of your headset until it feels secure and comfortable. A headset with a loose fit can shift during calls; one that's too tight causes discomfort during long sessions. If your headset has a click-stop or locking mechanism, secure your preferred length. 2. Position the microphone correctly Place your microphone approximately two fingers' distance from the corner of your mouth. Use both hands when shaping the boom arm into position. Once set, avoid adjusting the microphone during a call; moving it mid-conversation can cause audio level fluctuations. 3. Avoid incorrect placement Never place the microphone directly in front of your mouth, beneath your nostrils, or in contact with your lips or face. These positions cause distortion, breath noise, or inconsistent audio capture. Voice techniques You don't need to modify your speaking style to get great results with Sanas. The following standard voice modulation techniques are about being consistent and clear. Speak at your natural pace Try to speak in your natural conversational speed. Speaking too fast can result in unclear audio and force your recipient to ask you to repeat yourself. Speaking unnaturally slowly can make the conversation feel disengaged. Find your natural rhythm and maintain it throughout the call. Articulate clearly Pronounce words fully and clearly and avoid mumbling or trailing off at the end of sentences. Take natural pauses between sentences to maintain a steady speech flow. Keep in mind: Sanas enhances how your voice sounds, but it can't correct mispronunciations or grammar. Focus on using correct pronunciation and clear sentence structure during your calls. For example, pronounce "vehicle" as "vee-uh-kul," not "vy-kul." Maintain a consistent volume Speak at an adequate volume and hold that level throughout the call. Volume fluctuations make it harder for Sanas to process your audio consistently and can create an unpleasant experience for your recipient. Manage your breathing Take breaths between sentences, not in the middle of them. Avoid heavy breathing while speaking — steady, controlled breathing helps maintain a natural rhythm and prevents breath noise from being picked up by the microphone. Do's and don'ts These habits will help you get the best results from Sanas, day in and day out: Do’s Don’ts Restart your computer daily. A daily restart prevents performance issues from building up over time and keeps the Sanas App running smoothly. Avoid wrong audio sources on your softphone. Your softphone's audio sources must be set to the Sanas audio devices and not to your headset directly. The correct configuration depends on your Sanas product. Refer to the Sanas App user guide for the exact settings for your setup. Verify your Sanas App configuration at the start of each session. Before your first call of the day, confirm that your Sanas product and its controls are enabled with the correct audio configuration. A quick 30-second check can save you from issues mid-call. Avoid using an external webcam microphone or built-in laptop microphone. These audio sources pick up too much ambient noise and lack the quality needed for Sanas to process your voice effectively. Always use your USB headset as the audio input. Disable built-in speech enhancement and noise suppression in your conferencing app. Features like Zoom's "Background noise removal" or Teams' "Noise suppression" can interfere with Sanas audio processing. Disable or minimize these settings in your softphone to let Sanas handle audio enhancement without conflicts. Do not close the Sanas App during a live call. Closing the Sanas app (not minimizing) stops the audio processing immediately. Your call continues, but your recipient will notice the change. If you accidentally close the app, relaunch it and sign in again to resume processing. Always use a USB-based headset. USB headsets p
