pages.title: Deploy Sanas App on Stratodesk NoTouch OS
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Stratodesk NoTouch OS is a Linux-based read-only system, and the app deployment happens via the app distribution link. The advantages of the link-based distribution are that you receive the latest features and updates from Sanas, available without the need for manual app updates from the Admin or the app user. This guide provides detailed instructions on deploying the Sanas App on a computer running NoTouch OS. Before you begin NoTouch Center access : NoTouch Center is the centrally managed control center for the app deployment. You’ll need admin access to the NoTouch Center to proceed with the procedure. Os version : Stratodesk provides prebuilt support for the Sanas App on the following app versions: NoTouch OS 3.7.154 and above NoTouch Center 4.5.696 and above Deployment Get the Sanas app link. Contact Sanas Support to get your app distribution link. This is required for the app deployment. Configure the app distribution link on NoTouch Center. Access the NoTouch OS center and log in with your credentials. Note: Sanas works with both server (VDI) or self hosted NoTouch OS. Navigate to the Group Settings from the left-side menu. Click New Connection in the selected group settings. Select Sanas under the Connection Mode. Enter the app deployment link you received from Sanas under Connection target Configure the app deployment timeline by: Enable the Automatic start at system reboot Enable the icon on desktop Click Save to apply the changes. Click Announce to deploy the app to all connected endpoints (computers). For App users on Stratodesk, ensure you configure the following: App authentication mode : Configure the authentication mode to UAK. Refer Authentication mode to learn more. Add app user : The App users will require the User ID and Group ID to authenticate. Refer to Add app user for instructions on adding users. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Update the Installer ID on a User's Computer
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Installer IDs are unique identifiers assigned to each group and the Sanas Account. When updated on a user's machine, the Installer ID helps Sanas pre-configure the app based on the user’s group configuration and enables auto-provisioning when using app authentication modes such as Auto-activation and Single-Sign On. Installer IDs are relevant only for Sanas App users. Learn more about the available authentication modes for the Sanas App users. How it works The Installer ID serves two purposes during App activation: Group identification — Sanas uses the Installer ID to identify the group the user belongs to, then pre-configures the App based on that group's settings (language, accent, authentication mode, etc.). Auto-provisioning — When a user activates the App for the first time, Sanas checks whether the user exists in the group associated with the Installer ID. If the user exists, they are granted access. If not, Sanas automatically creates the user in that group and grants access. Ensure the Auto Provisioning toggle is enabled on the intended groups. Navigate to Settings Configuration Application Authentication Ensure SSO or Auto-activation is configured > Ensure the Automatic User Creation toggle is enabled Locate the Installer ID Each group has a unique Installer ID. To find it: Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Navigate to the Get Sanas page. Select the group for which you need the Installer ID. Copy the Installer ID and save it securely. Tip: Use your Sanas Account's Installer ID to provision all App users directly to the Default Group of your Account. Once added, you can move users to their respective groups as needed. See Move App Users for instructions. Before you begin Ensure you have access to the user's machine to update the Installer ID, either directly or through your endpoint management software. Ensure you have copied the correct Installer ID for the target group from the Get Sanas page on the Portal. Update the Installer ID The Installer ID can be updated at two stages: During installation — Set the Installer ID as part of the initial app installation. Post installation — Update the Installer ID on machines where the app is already installed. Choose the applicable stage, platform, and method below. During the Sanas App installation Note: The below command can also run through endpoint management software to update installer IDs on centrally managed user machines. Windows macOS Method 1 App installer Enter the installer ID in its respective field when prompted during installation. Method 2 Command Note: Replace the placeholders <file_path> and <installer_ID> with the actual values. For example, here is a sample command for msi file type: msiexec /i "C:\Users\Acme_inc\Downloads\Sanas-5.2.11-x64.msi" installerid="XXXX-XXXX-XXXX" /q .msi installer (Valid to execute via CMD or PowerShell) msiexec /i "<file_path>" installerid="<installer_ID>" /q .exe installer (CMD) "<file_path>" /installerid="<installer_ID>" /q (PowerShell) & "<file_path>" /installerid="<installer_ID>" /q Method 1 App installer Enter the installer ID in its respective field when prompted during installation. Method 2: Terminal Note: Replace the placeholders <file_path> and <installer_ID> with the actual values. Run the following commands in the same order: sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/ai.sanas.SanasApp.plist InstallerId "<installer_ID>" sudo installer -pkg <file_path> -target / Post Sanas App installation Note: The below command can also run through endpoint management software to update installer IDs on centrally managed user machines. Windows macOS Note: Replace the placeholders <installer_ID> with the actual value. (Valid to execute via CMD or PowerShell) reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Sanas.ai\Sanas" /v InstallerId /t REG_SZ /d "<installer_ID>" Note: Replace the placeholders <file_path> and <installer_ID> with the actual values. Run the following commands in the same order: sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/ai.sanas.SanasApp.plist InstallerId "<installer_ID>" Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure Single-Sign On (SSO) for Sanas App/ Portal
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Configure Single Sign-On (SSO) to allow users to authenticate on the Sanas Portal and the Sanas App using your organization's existing Identity Provider (IdP). Sanas uses the SAML 2.0 protocol to integrate with your IdP for authentication and access validation. How it works SSO follows the following workflow to authenticate users: The user navigates to the Sanas Portal or App. User authentication: Sanas Portal : User selects the SSO option on the login screen to initiate authentication. Sanas App : User gets automatically redirected for authentication upon the Sanas App launch. The user is redirected to the organization's IdP and follows the on-screen instructions to complete authentication. Upon successful verification, the user is redirected back to Sanas with authorized access. Note: The user must exist on the integrated IdP. Automatic User Creation Automatic User Creation is an additional feature that works alongside Auto-Activation and SSO to eliminate the requirement of manually adding users to the Portal. When Automatic User Creation is enabled, Sanas checks whether the user exists on the Portal and acts accordingly: If the user exists , the user is granted access to the Sanas App. If the user does not exist , a new user account is created on the Portal, and the user is granted access to the Sanas App. Newly created users are mapped to a Group based on the Installer ID configured on their computer. Installer IDs are unique Group identifiers found on each group's Get Sanas page. There are two types: Group Installer ID — New users are added to the specific group associated with this ID. Account Installer ID — New users are added to the Default Group. Before you begin For Portal configuration, ensure your Portal role has Group Settings and Account Settings: Full access If configuring SSO for Sanas App users, ensure the Installer ID has been updated on each user's machine during app installation. If not, see Update Installer ID for instructions. Ensure the Auto-provisioning is enabled on the intended groups. Navigate to Settings Configuration Application Authentication Ensure SSO or Auto-activation is configured > Ensure the Automatic User Creation toggle is enabled Ensure you have administrative privileges on your IdP platform to complete the integration. Ensure all intended users are added to the IdP before enabling SSO. Ensure all intended Portal users are added to the Sanas Portal before enabling SSO. See Manage Portal Users for instructions. Configure SSO Follow the steps below to configure SSO: Step 1: Gather integration details from the Sanas Portal Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Navigate to Settings > Configuration > SSO Settings Click Add SSO Provider Enter your IdP name. Copy the following details and save them securely — you'll need these to complete the integration on your IdP: Identifier Reply URL Gather integration details from the Portal. Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Navigate to Settings Configuration SSO Settings Click Add SSO provider Enter an SSO name. Copy the following details and save them securely. We will need these details for the integration: Identifier Reply URL Step 2: Complete the SAML 2.0 integration on your IdP Configure the SAML integration on your IdP platform using the Identifier and Reply URL copied in Step 1. Map the following attributes during the SSO configuration: Attribute Value Description username UserID or Email Unique identifier for the user. name User name Display name for the user. Once the integration is complete, download or copy the X-509 certificate metadata from your IdP. You'll need this to finalize the configuration on the Sanas Portal. Below are reference resources for common IdP platforms: Okta Microsoft Entra ID Step 3: Complete the SSO configuration on the Sanas Portal If you downloaded the X-509 certificate as a file, open it in a text editor and copy its content. Return to the SSO Settings page on the Sanas Portal and paste the certificate content. pages.title: Configure Auto-Activation for Sanas App
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Auto-Activation is an app authentication mode that does not require any manual credential entry from the user. Instead, it verifies a user's access to the Sanas App using the following computer details: Connected organization domain (Windows) Host name (macOS) Logged-in user profile If the above details match an active user on the Portal, the user automatically gets access to the Sanas App. How it works When Auto-Activation is configured, Sanas verifies the user's access in real time upon app launch using their computer details. Upon successful verification, a new app session starts automatically — no manual login required. Automatic User Creation Automatic User Creation is an additional feature that works alongside Auto-Activation and SSO to eliminate the requirement of manually adding users to the Portal. When Automatic User Creation is enabled, Sanas checks whether the user exists on the Portal and acts accordingly: If the user exists , the user is granted access to the Sanas App. If the user does not exist , a new user account is created on the Portal, and the user is granted access to the Sanas App. Newly created users are mapped to a Group based on the Installer ID configured on their computer. Installer IDs are unique Group identifiers found on each group's Get Sanas page. There are two types: Group Installer ID — New users are added to the specific group associated with this ID. Account Installer ID — New users are added to the Default Group. Before you begin Ensure your Portal role has Group Settings or Account Settings: Full Access to configure the authentication mode for a group or the entire account. Ensure the correct Installer IDs are configured on all intended users' computers before enabling Auto-Activation. For instructions, see update installer ID Configure Auto-activation Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. On the Group Tree , select the group you want to configure. To apply Auto-Activation across all groups, select your Sanas Account instead. Go to Settings > Configuration > Application Authentication Select Auto Activation , then click Save (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle to prevent subgroups from modifying the authentication mode. Confirm that Auto-provisioning is enabled: The Automatic User Creation toggle is vissible only when you’ve configured Auto-activation as your preffered authetnication mode. Verify that the Automatic User Creation toggle is enabled. (Optional) Enable the Lock Configuration toggle to prevent subgroups from modifying Auto-provisioning. Note: If you have existing App users who are currently active on the Portal, ask them to end their current session and relaunch the Sanas App to authenticate via Auto-Activation. Additionally, group administrators should review and deactivate any previously created user accounts to prevent duplicate entries within the group. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.text: summary Prev Next Discover our latest innovations, enhancements, and fixes deployed this month. What’s Released On-Demand Model Updates — Update AI models instantly without reinstalling the app. Sanas Mac App Download — Portal Admins can now download the Sanas Mac app directly from the portal. 1. On-Demand Model Updates: Update AI Models Without Downtime Note : The on-demanad model update feature is currently available only on Windows. We've fundamentally changed how you manage Sanas apps. AI models now update independently from the core application, giving you control, flexibility, and zero disruption to your operations. What changed The Sanas app has two components: the AI model and the application. Previously, these were locked together—updating one meant reinstalling everything. Now they're separate. Switch AI models as needed without touching the application itself. Why this matters Reduced IT overhead : Deploy once with a single installer. No more managing multiple app versions across teams Faster time-to-value : New models reach users in hours, not days Business continuity : Users maintain complete Noise Cancellation and Accent Translation access during updates—no workflow interruption. Note : The accent translation becomes temporarily unavailable to users only when the workspace's configured accents require a different AI model, while noise cancellation remains operational. Key capabilities Single Unified Installer - One installer serves your entire organization—Configure models per workspace by selecting source and target accents. Background Updates - Models download automatically based on your preferences. Users continue working—the new model activates without any action needed from the app user No Reinstallation - Models update within the app: no user disruption and no deployment coordination. How It Works The system automatically ensures users have the right model for their workspace configuration. Case 1: New Workspace Setup Create workspace : Specify source and target accents in your workspace creation request. Deploy app : Download from the Download App page and deploy to user machines. Auto-verification : Sanas checks if the deployed model matches your accent configuration. If not, it initiates an automatic model switch. Background update : The correct model downloads and activates without disrupting the app usage. Case 2: Updating Existing Workspaces Change accents : Update source and/or target accents for any workspace (see Configure Workspace Accents ). Auto-verification : Sanas detects the change and updates models automatically using the same process above. Case 3: Choosing Specific Models By default, Sanas recommends optimal models for your configuration. You can override this and select any available model. Switch to Stable Models Configure auto-update : Enable auto updates ( setup guide ). Select models : Go to Download App , click Edit , and choose your preferred models. Deploy : Click Start Auto Update . The new selected AI model gets deployed. Switch to Beta Models ⚠️ Beta Models Notice ccess upcoming AI models and associated features before they are released to everyone. Enable Experimental Features in Settings to access Beta models, then follow the steps above to switch models. Understanding Update Types App Updates : New features, UI improvements, and bug fixes to the core application. Model Updates : AI model changes to match workspace accent configurations. These updates happen automatically when you create or modify workspaces. Both update types use the same unified installer—you never need multiple versions. Getting Started Requirements : Sanas app version 4.4.X or higher Download App Download page Next steps Deploy the latest app version across your organization Configure workspace accents as needed Enable auto-update preferences for seamless model updates. 2. Sanas macOS app availability Portal Admins can now download the Sanas Mac app directly from the portal Download App page. Note: The On-Demand Model Updates feature currently applies only to Windows Getting Started on Mac: Follow our Quick Start guide and use the macOS instructions to set up and start using Sanas on your macOS. The AVO detects any sudden volume amplification in the speaker's volume during the call. It automatically adjusts the volume to a comfortable range before it reaches the recipient, resulting in a smoother, distortion-free, and professional-grade calling experience. What It Offers Expanded Range of Support Headsets : AVO optimizes the common inconsistent volume fluctuations issue on headsets, making Sanas compatible with a larger range of headsets than ever before 🔊 Smoother Calling Experience : AVO fine-tunes speaker volume automatically to deliver professional-quality audio output ⚡ Seamless Integration : Operates in the background with zero user intervention required. Enable AVO for a Workspace First, the admin enables the AVO feature for a workspace from the Sanas Portal: Portal > Settings > Automatic Volume Optimization . pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This monthly update document covers all the new features and updates released for Sanas SDKs. In this release; Added support for new source and target accents Added Sanas personalisation functionality to the Sanas SDK. Sanas personalisation lets users preserve their voice identity in their accent translated voice, making it sound more natural and distinct. 1. Unlocked new source and target accents Available for : Accent Translation Supported platforms : Sanas Windows SDK SDK version 1.5.3 and 1.5.4 Our latest Windows SDK versions now support a new source and target accent for users of the accent translation. Windows SDK versions Type New accents Description 1.5.3 Source AFRME (African and Middle East) Source accent is the geographic English accent of the Sanas app user. Note : The target accents remain the United States 1.5.4 Target UK (United Kingdom) Target accent is the recipient's geographic English accent. Note : The source accents are India the Philippines Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East. Get started A fresh integration of the applicable SDK package is required to enable the specific source or target accents. Contact our support team to get access to the latest SDK packages. 2. Sanas personalisation Available for : Accent Translation users Supported platforms : Sanas Windows SDK SDK version 1.5.2 We're thrilled to introduce Sanas Personalisation —a powerful new feature that lets you maintain your unique voice identity while using Accent Translation. Now you can sound both global and authentically you. Why this matters Preserve your voice identity. You'll sound global and confident without losing what makes your voice distinctive. Enhanced naturalness. Your personalized voice not only sounds global but also retains the speech nuances from your original voice, further enhancing your accent-translated voice. How it works Feature enablement - Workspace admins enable Sanas Personalisation from the workspace’s settings page. Once enabled, SDK users on the supported version will see the personalisation feature available. Voice profile creation - Users create their voice profile in just a few minutes. The following modes are available for voice profile creation: Automatic : Doesn’t require the user to record their voice manually; instead, Sanas samples the user’s voice during the call. The profile gets created and gets applied on the next call. Manual : Allow user to record their voice offline to create a voice profile. The profile gets applied to the next app session. Build UI to facilitate voice recording. Build a UI in your custom app to enable voice recording in manual mode. Automatic mode doesn’t require that. Admin visibility - Admins can track personalisation status for each team member on the Users page, showing status as "Completed" or "Not completed." Flexible updates - If required, users can overwrite their previously created voice profiles. Record a new voice profile to overwrite the previous one. The new profile gets automatically applied on the next app session. Works everywhere - Voice profile syncs across devices, so you get the same personalized experience whether you're using Sanas from your laptop or another machine. Additional notes We are using the Wav2Identity model to create voice profiles. Recording is capped at 1 minute. The recorded audio is not stored in our system and is destroyed after processing. Personalised voice profiles are saved in the backend and auto-applied on the next startup. Documentation Admin : Refer to enable Sanas personalisatio n feature for detailed instructions for the admin. Developer : Refer to the changelog document added along with the release files to learn more about the newly added API schema. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Best Practices: Accent Translation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This user guide provides clear instructions This guide is for Sanas App users who want to get the clearest, most consistent audio experience on every call. Whether you're just getting started or refining your setup, following these practices will help Sanas perform at its best. Sections covered: Microphone positioning — How to position your headset microphone for optimal audio capture Voice modulation techniques — Speaking habits that improve Sanas’ output quality Do's and Don'ts — A quick checklist to use at the start of each session Audio configurations — How to configure your softphone's audio settings for Sanas Regular maintenance — Routine steps to keep Sanas running smoothly. Video guide null Microphone positioning Correct microphone positioning directly impacts how well Sanas captures your speech. Consistent placement ensures stable audio levels and reduces processing errors. Headset fit Adjust your headset to achieve a comfortable, secure fit. If your headset includes a length-locking mechanism (such as a click-stop), use it to maintain a consistent fit across sessions. Avoid a fit that is too loose or too tight, especially during long usage sessions. Optimal microphone position Position your microphone approximately two fingers away from the corner of your mouth. Use both hands to shape the boom arm into position. Once set, avoid adjusting the microphone during an active call, as repositioning can cause audio level fluctuations. Positions to avoid Do not place the microphone directly in front of your mouth, underneath your nostrils, or in contact with your lips or face. Voice modulation techniques How you speak has a direct impact on Sanas output quality. Follow these techniques for the clearest results: 1. Speak at your natural pace Speaking too fast can cause unclear output and repetitions; speaking too slowly can reduce engagement. 2. Maintain a natural breathing rhythm Avoid heavy breathing while speaking. Use natural pauses between sentences to breathe. 3. Articulate clearly and completely Pronounce words fully and avoid mumbling or indistinct speech. Take natural pauses between sentences to maintain a smooth speech flow. 4. Try maintaining a consistent volume level Speak at an adequate volume and keep that level steady throughout the call. 5. Always practice using proper grammar Practicing good grammar generally improves clarity and reduces the likelihood of misunderstandings. Aim for clear, appropriately structured language suited to your audience and context. Do’s and Don’ts Use this checklist at the start of each Sanas session. Do’s Dont’s Restart your computer daily to prevent performance issues. Do not use a laptop's internal microphone or an external webcam microphone. Verify your Sanas App configuration at the start of each session. Refer to the Sanas App User Guide for instructions. Do not use analog or Bluetooth headsets. Always use a USB headset for the best audio quality. Use a USB headset at all times. Do not close the Sanas App during an active call. Disable any built-in speech enhancement features in your softphone. Do not speak too fast, too slowly, or at an inconsistent volume. Configure your softphone's audio sources correctly at the start of each session. See Audio Configurations below. Do not reposition your microphone during an active call. Follow the voice modulation techniques outlined in this guide. Do not ignore update notifications — install Sanas App updates promptly. Audio configurations Sanas relies on its dedicated audio drivers, called Sanas devices , to route audio streams through the Sanas App. Your softphone must be configured to use the Sanas devices to allow Sanas to operate unintrupted. Configure your softphone's audio settings based on the features available in your Sanas App. Accent Translation with Inbound Noise Cancellation Accent Translation only Audio sources Windows macOS Input Sanas Audio Sanas Microphone Output Sanas Audio Sanas Speaker Audio sources Windows macOS Input Sanas Audio Sanas Microphone Note: No need for configuring Sanas device for the output audio on Accent Translation only mode. Regular maintenance techniques Routine maintenance keeps the Sanas App running efficiently and prevents performance degradation over time. Restart your computer daily to close background processes and free up system resources. Clear temporary files regularly to avoid unnecessary storage buildup. Install app updates as soon as you receive

pages.title: Sanas App Update
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction App updates ensure that your Sanas app stays current with the latest features, performance improvements, and security enhancements. Most updates are deployed in the background by your IT team and typically require no action from you. However, if your admin has enabled the Auto Update feature, you will receive a notification when an update is available. You can then choose to install the update at a convenient time—within the scheduled update window—without interrupting your daily work. Before You Begin Please keep the following in mind before proceeding with an update: Update notifications appear only after you launch the Sanas app. Avoid updating during an active call to prevent service interruptions. Ensure a stable internet connection to download the update smoothly. Understanding App Update Notifications You may encounter different types of update notifications depending on how your admin has configured the auto update. Scheduled App Update If an app update has been scheduled, you will see notifications on both your desktop and within the Sanas app. These will inform you of the upcoming update and when it will be available. Example Notification s: Desktop Notification Sanas App Notification You don’t need to take any action until the update becomes available. App Update Available If you access the app during the update window, you will receive a notification that the update is ready to install. You can begin the update process by clicking Update Now from either the desktop or an in-app notification. Example Notifications Desktop Notification Sanas App Notification The update will remain available throughout the scheduled update duration. Forced App Update If the update is mandatory, you’ll receive a notification indicating that it will be installed automatically during the scheduled time if not initiated manually. You can still choose to click Update Now to start the update immediately. Example Notifications: Desktop Notification Sanas App Notification If no action is taken, the update will begin automatically within the defined update window. Need Help? Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Issues Related to Audio: Accent Translation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide walks you through verifying that your headset, system audio, and Sanas App are correctly configured. Running through these steps before each Sanas usage session helps prevent the most common audio issues during calls. How Sanas works The Sanas App needs continuous access to your audio stream to process and enhance your voice in real time. To enable this, your softphone must use the Sanas device as its audio input source, and the Sanas App must use your headset as its microphone input. Incorrect configuration at either point is the most common cause of audio issues. Before you begin Ensure the Sanas App is installed and you have active access. Use a USB-connected headset for the best audio quality. You may need administrator access to modify softphone audio configurations. Verification steps Run through the following checks: Ensure you have a stable network connection with low latency and minimal packet loss. Poor network conditions can cause jittery or distorted audio. Verify that your computer is not under a high CPU or memory load, as this can affect real-time audio processing. Windows macOS Open Task Manager and check CPU and memory usage under the Performance tab. Close unnecessary background applications to reduce load. Restart your computer regularly to avoid this issue. Open Activity Monitor and check CPU and memory usage. Close unnecessary background applications to reduce load. Restart your computer regularly to avoid this issue. Verify the headset's physical condition and confirm its audio drivers are up to date. A faulty headset or outdated drivers can cause audio issues independent of Sanas. Disable any built-in noise cancellation or audio enhancement features in your softphone. These features interfere with Sanas and can cause distortion. Audio configuration steps Follow the steps below to verify audio configuration on the Sanas App and your softphone. Sanas App Open the Sanas App and confirm the following audio device selections: Incoming Audio (microphone): Your headset's microphone. Outgoing Audio (speaker): Your headset's earphones. Note: Avoid selecting a built-in microphone or external webcam’s microphone as the audio source. Confirm the Accent Translation toggle is turned on and remains on for the duration of your call. Softphone In your softphone's audio settings, confirm the following Sanas devices are selected: Note: The output Sanas device is only required if your Sanas App has Outbound Noise Cancellation enabled. Audio Windows macOS Input Sanas Audio Sanas Microphone Output Sanas Audio Sanas Speaker Info: If you are running an older Sanas App version, the device names may appear as Sanas Virtual Microphone or Sanas Virtual Speaker Verify your system audio settings to confirm that the microphone and speaker are unmuted and volume levels are set adequately. Windows macOS Open Sound Settings from the Windows Start Menu and click More sound settings under the Advanced section. In the Playback tab, right-click your headset and select Set as Default Device Select your headset, click Properties Levels tab. Set the volume to between 50% and 70% , confirm the device is not muted, and set Sidetone to a low audible level if available. Click OK In the Recording tab, select Sanas Audio , click Properties Listen tab. Select the checkbox for Listen to this device , speak into your headset, and confirm that a green audio signal appears. Uncheck Listen to this device and click OK Open System Settings Sound Under the Output tab, select your headset and confirm the volume is set adequately high, and the device is not muted. Under the Input tab, select Sanas Microphone and confirm that the input volume is set adequately high. Perform a test call with Sanas enabled and confirm the audio is clear. Validate on a live call rather than a recording, as recordings are often compressed and may not reflect real-time audio quality. Tip: For microphone technique and headset positioning guidance, see the Best Practices Guide Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Issues Related to Sanas App Installation on Windows
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Installing or updating the Sanas app on Windows is typically straightforward. However, you may occasionally run into errors during installation or manual updates. These issues are usually caused by missing administrator privileges or entering an incorrect Installer ID. This guide walks you through the most common issues and how to resolve them. Installation via Windows Installer (GUI Method) 1. Missing Administrator Privileges Issue: Installation fails or doesn't proceed as expected. Solution: Right-click the downloaded Sanas installer file. Click Run as administrator Click Yes in the confirmation pop-up. If prompted, enter your computer’s administrator password. Note : Granting admin privileges is necessary for successful installation. 2. Parallel Installation Running Issue: Another installation process is already running in the background, causing a conflict. Solution: Restart your computer to terminate any ongoing background installations. Once restarted, try installing the Sanas app again. 3. Incorrect Installer ID Issue: The installer displays an error due to an invalid or mismatched Installer ID. Solution: Ensure you’re using the correct Installer ID associated with your Workspace. To find it: Go to the Sanas Portal and log in. Use the Workspace Switcher to select your Workspace. Click Download App in the navigation menu. Click Copy Installer ID – this will copy the correct ID to your clipboard. Paste the Installer ID into the installer wizard when prompted. Note : Installer IDs are unique to each Workspace. Using one from another Workspace will result in an error. Installation via CLI (Command-Line Interface Method) 1. Launching Command Prompt Without Admin Rights Issue: The installation command fails or is blocked. Solution: Search for Command Prompt from the Windows Start Menu. Right-click the Command Prompt icon. Select Run as administrator Click Yes in the confirmation window. Enter your admin password if prompted. Note : Always launch Command Prompt with administrator privileges when using the CLI installation method. 2. Using Placeholder Values in the Command Issue: Placeholder text not replaced in the command results in a failed installation. Solution: Update the CLI command with actual values before running it. Example Command for Accent Translation App: powershellCopyEdit"SanasAccenttranslator-V2-2.XX.XXXX.X-XXX-prod.exe" INSTALLERID="XXXX-XXXX-XXXX" /qb Replace the placeholders as follows: App Version: Go to the folder where the Sanas installer was downloaded. Copy the exact filename (e.g., SanasAccenttranslator-V2-2.35.1024.1-001-prod.exe ). Replace SanasAccenttranslator-V2-2.XX.XXXX.X-XXX-prod.exe With the correct filename. Installer ID: Get the correct Installer ID from your Sanas Workspace as shown above Replace "XXXX-XXXX-XXXX" with the actual Installer ID in the command. Final Example (after replacing placeholders): powershellCopyEdit"SanasAccenttranslator-V2-2.35.1024.1-001-prod.exe" INSTALLERID="A1B2-C3D4-E5F6" /qb Note : Double-check the values before executing to avoid installation failures. Need Help? Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Overview: Sanas Noise Cancellation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide provides a detailed overview of the Sanas Noise Cancellation NC ) app. Sanas NC is a multi-platform-supported application that helps you utilize NC capabilities along with your calls in real time. The NC app is bundled with our advanced speech understanding AI models to remove background noises captured by your headset’s microphone securely and in real time. All audio processing for noise cancellation happens locally (on-device), always ensuring a secure and crystal-clear calling experience. Overview The Sanas NC app contains the following pages: Home screen The Home screen page hosts the main app configuration options: Note : The admins control the Noise Cancellation toggle’s functionality on the Sanas NC app. If configured, you may not be able to manually disable the NC toggles from the NC app. NC for incoming & outgoing audio NC for outgoing audio Noise Cancellation Microphone: Controls the Noise Cancellation for your microphone. Enabling this applies noise cancellation to the outgoing audio. Outgoing Audio: Select the audio input source for outgoing audio. Typically, the microphone of your connected headset. Noise Cancellation Speaker : Controls the Noise Cancellation for your speaker. Enabling this applies noise cancellation to the incoming audio. Incoming Audio : Select the audio output source for the incoming audio. Typically, the earphones of your connected headset. Minimize App: Minimizes the app widget. App Menu: Opens the app menu. Noise Cancellation: Enable or disable Noise Cancellation for your microphone. This feature eliminates background noise captured by your headset’s microphone during a call. Audio input: Selects the audio input source. Typically, your connected headset’s microphone. Minimize app: Minimizes the app widget. App menu: Opens the app menu. Help, Feedback & About Help : View system performance indicators such as CPU, memory, and battery status. For troubleshooting, use Restart Audio or Check Compatibility Feedback : Share your experience and report issues via a quick rating and feedback form. About : Displays installed app details, including version and copyright information. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: App User Guide: Noise Cancellation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide walks you through setting up and using the Sanas desktop app with Noise cancellation (NC). New to Sanas? Take a short tour of the Sanas app to learn about its controls and options. A quick summary of what you'll do: Activate the Sanas app Configure your audio settings Set up your calling app Before you begin Make sure you have: Sanas app installed - If you don't see it on your computer, request your IT admin for installation. USB Headset - Use a USB headset for the best audio quality. Network login - Make sure your computer is connected to your organization's domain, and you're logged in with your user profile. This is required for auto-activation to work if your organization has enabled it. Internet connection - Sanas processes audio on your device, but it needs an internet connection to verify your access. Step 1: Activate your app Auto-activation UAK If your organization has enabled Auto-activation: Launch the Sanas app. The app logs you in automatically. Quick troubleshooting - Ensure your computer is connected to your organization's domain, and you're logged in with your user profile before launching the Sanas app. Try relaunching to reattempt auto activation. If this doesn't work, you can try activating via the UAK method. If you see an activation screen: Enter your Workspace ID and User ID Note : Your admin should have sent these credentials to you. If not, contact your admin. Click Activate Key If you see a session conflict Sanas allows only one active session per license. If Sanas is already running on another device, you'll see the message: "Existing user session identified." Click Continue to close the other session and start a new one on this device. Make sure Sanas isn't being used on an active call before doing this. Step 2: Configure your Sanas app Your Sanas app version determines your app controls interface. To check your app version: click the menu (top-left corner) → About For app version 4.0 and above Sanas app version 4.0 and above has two possible configurations: Omnidirectional Noise Cancellation Outbound Noise Cancellation Only If you see toggles for both Microphone and Speaker: Noise Cancellation Microphone – Keep the toggle ON to remove background noise from your speech. Microphone Input – Select your headset from the dropdown. Noise Cancellation Speaker – Keep the toggle ON to remove noise from the caller's side (what you hear). Speaker Output – Select your headset from the dropdown. If you see only one toggle for the Microphone: Noise Cancellation Microphone – Keep ON during all calls. Microphone Input – Select your headset from the dropdown. Step 3: Set up your calling application Configure your softphone or video app (e.g., Zoom, Teams) to use Sanas. These settings are usually applied automatically, but verify them before each session. In your calling app's audio settings, set: Setting Select Microphone / Input Sanas Virtual Audio or Sanas Virtual Microphone Speaker / Output Sanas Virtual Speaker Select only if the Noise Cancellation for both the microphone and speaker is available, and skip selecting for the microphone-only mode (shown under Outbound Noise Cancellation). Example (Zoom): Go to Settings → Audio , then select " Sanas Virtual Audio " as your microphone and " Sanas Virtual Speaker " as your speaker. For app-specific instructions, see: Web-based softphones Application-based softphones Make a test call Before using Sanas on real calls, make a test call to confirm everything works. If something sounds off, double-check that the correct audio devices are selected in both Sanas and your calling app. FAQ What if I don't see "Sanas Virtual Audio" in my calling app? If Sanas devices aren't showing up: Make sure the Sanas app is running and your headset is connected. Restart your calling application. The devices should appear if Sanas is running and your microphone is selected as the audio input source on the app. If still missing, contact your admin. What if I have audio issues during a call? pages.title: Best practices: Noise Cancellation
pages.text: summary Prev Next This guide outlines best practices for using the Sanas app, ensuring seamless integration with your existing workflow and delivering the most natural, consistent audio quality. null 🎧 Microphone Positioning The position of your headset's microphone is one of the most critical aspects in capturing your audio while you speak. Incorrect positioning can result in the omission of certain audio sections when pitch and frequency vary. 1. Adjust the headset to the correct length Wear the headset and adjust its headband length to achieve a comfortable fit. Do not wear your headset too loose or too tight to avoid any discomfort during extended calling sessions. Secure your preferred headband length if your headset has a click-stop or another locking mechanism. Headset positioning 2. Optimal microphone position Position your microphone at approximately two-finger distance away from your mouth's corner. Use both hands while shaping your microphone's boom arm. Avoid changing the microphone position during an ongoing call to prevent any possible audio level fluctuations. Microphone positioning 3. Avoid incorrect microphone placement Never place the microphone directly in front of your mouth, underneath your nostrils, or in contact with your lips or face. Incorrect microphone placement 🗣️ Voice Modulation Techniques You can achieve great results with Sanas by following these simple voice modulation techniques: 1. Speak at your natural pace Always try to speak at your natural pace. Speaking fast may result in unclear messages and repetition, while speaking unnaturally slowly may lack engagement in the conversation. Practice maintaining a consistent pace throughout your calling sessions. 2. Articulate clearly Pronounce words correctly and completely without mumbling or indistinct pronunciation for clear communication. Always take pauses between sentences and maintain a natural speech flow. 3. Maintain adequate volume Speak at an adequate volume and maintain that level throughout the call to clearly distinguish your voice from background noise. Audio level fluctuations often lead to an unpleasant calling experience for recipients. 4. Manage breathing Take breaths between sentences and avoid taking them in between. Avoid heavy breathing while speaking and maintain a steady rhythm during your conversations. ✔️ Do's and Don'ts This section highlights a few key habits you can adapt for the best results with Sanas. ✅ Things to DO Restart your computer daily. Prevents any performance issues. Verify your Sanas app configurations. Check at the beginning of each app session Ensure Sanas remains enabled, and the correct audio input is selected. Disable the built-in noise suppression features. Disable any built-in noise suppression feature on your used softphone, if available, to avoid audio input interference. Use high-quality headsets always. Always use USB connection-based high-quality headsets Avoid headsets with analog or Bluetooth connections, as USB connections provide better audio quality We recommend periodically testing your headsets by performing a demo call to identify any hardware defects and avoid issues during a live call. 🚫 Don't Do Select the following audio sources: Input : Sanas Virtual Microphone Output : Headset’s earphones Never use an external webcam microphone or the system's built-in array microphone. Do not use these as your audio input source. Do not close the Sanas application during an ongoing call. Closing the app mid-call can cause audio issues and leave the recipient with a bad experience. What's Next? You now know all the best practices you'll need for crystal clear calls. Refer to the Sanas user guide to get started with Noise Cancellation.

pages.title: Troubleshoot audio misconfiguration: Noise Cancellation
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction While most users enjoy a smooth experience with the Sanas application, you might occasionally encounter unusual behavior. Misconfigured system audio settings often cause these issues. This guide will help you identify and fix common audio-related issues that can affect the Sanas app's performance. The latest versions of the Sanas app automatically configure most audio settings during installation. However, some softphones may require manual configuration. Before you begin, make sure: The Sanas app is installed, launched, and activated. A high-quality (USB type) headset is connected to your computer. You have administrative access on your computer (some changes may require an admin password). 1. Muted Microphone Issue: The call recipient can’t hear your voice. This may be caused by your microphone being muted or set to a low volume level. Here’s how to fix it: Step 1: Check Headset Audio Levels Open Sound Settings from the Windows Start Menu. Scroll down and click More sound settings under the Advanced section. Go to the Playback tab. Select your connected headset and click Properties Under the Levels tab: Ensure the volume is set to an adequate level. Confirm that the device is not muted. (Optional) If you see the Sidetone option, set it to a low but audible level. Click OK to save changes. Step 2: Test the Sanas Microphone In the Sound settings , go to the Recording tab. Select Sanas Virtual Audio and click Properties Go to the Listen tab. Check the checkbox next to Listen to this device Speak into your microphone and verify that a green audio signal graph. Uncheck Listen to this device and click OK Restart the Sanas app and perform a test call. Sanas Support If the issue persists, contact the Sanas Support 2. Incorrect Audio Input Source Issue: You can’t hear the call recipient. This may happen if the Sanas Speaker is selected as the default playback device instead of your headset. How to Fix It: Open Sound Settings from the Windows Start Menu. Click More sound settings under the Advanced section. In the Playback tab: If Sanas Speaker is the default device, right-click your headset. Click Set as Default Device to switch audio output back to your headset. 3. Faulty Headset or Misconfiguration Issue: Voice echo during the call. Possible Causes & Solutions: Faulty Hardware: Try using a different headset to check if the issue persists. Audio Configuration Issue: Follow the instructions in the Muted Microphone section to ensure proper setup. Make a test call to verify improvements. Contact Support if the problem continues. 4. Not Following Sanas Best Practices Issue: Audio distortion or degradation during calls. Common Causes: Improper Use: Sanas performs best when best practices are followed, including: Proper headset positioning. Clear, steady speech patterns. Refer to the Best Practices Guide for more tips. Incorrect Audio Levels: Ensure your headset volume is set between 50% and 70%. Set Sidetone to a minimal level if available. Follow the steps from the Muted Microphone section for reconfiguration. 5. Sanas is Disabled in the App Issue: Accent Translation (AT) is not working. How to Fix It: On the Sanas home screen, ensure the Accent Translation toggle is turned on for the entire duration of your call. In your softphone’s audio input settings, ensure Sanas Microphone or Sanas Virtual Audio is selected. Refer to your softphone’s configuration guide for detailed steps. 6. Low volume output on the headset Issue: Low or no volume output on connected headset. How to fix it You can fix this issue by simply updating the system audio settings for your connected headset. You can follow the same steps mentioned under the Muted Microphone heading to update your headset’s audio settings. Need Help? Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

Deactivating a Team helps manage app licenses when specific teams are temporarily inactive. You can reactivate Teams at any time when they're operational again. Before you begin You’ll need Admin access on the Sanas Portal to manage Team status. Deactivate a Team Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu. Click the ellipsis menu button next to the Team you wish to deactivate, then click Deactivate ℹ️ Important : Team deactivation revoke the Sanas app access for all of its assigend users. Click Deactivate to confirm your action. The Team status gets updated Deactivated and moved to the last on the Teams list. Use the available pagination or search bar options to locate Teams. Reactivate a Team Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu. Click the ellipsis menu button next to the Team you wish to activate, then click Activate ℹ️ Important : Reactivation a team restores the Sanas app access for all of its assigned users. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Find Workspace details

pages.title: Add app users to a Team
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide provides clear instructions for adding app users to an existing Team using the following available methods: Add user via Portal : Use this method while adding fewer app user details Bulk upload app user details : Recommended while adding a larger group of app user details (up to 10,000 users). Add your app users to Teams to allow them to start using the Sanas app. You can group users logically based on their projects, geographical locations, work shifts, etc, to manage them and the app licenses effectively. Utilize the Teams filter in the Reports section to gain insight into team-specific app usage Note : Refer to the Create team guide if you need assistance with creating new teams in a Workspace. Exceptions for adding users While assigning app users to a Team is mandatory for granting them access to the Sanas app, you may not need to add their details under the following condition: Using auto-activation mode : If your Sanas Workspace uses the auto-activation mode for app activation (default on Sanas Noise Cancellation workspaces), the user's details are automatically added under the Workspace’s default Team upon the user's first app activation . If necessary, you can transfer app users between teams at any time Before you begin The following Sanas Portal users can add users to teams: Admin : Add users to any team under any Workspace Supervisor : Add users only to the assigned teams. Add app users’ details via the Sanas portal Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu, then click Add users Enter user details: User type : Ensure App User type is selected. Team : By default, the current team is selected. Change the assigned Team from the drop-down menu, if required. Identifiers : Enter a unique User ID and the name of the user. Ensure it meets the User ID criteria. ℹ️ Important : Ensure the entered User ID(s) meet the following criteria: - The user ID must not exceed the 64-character limit. - Avoid using following characters: < > & " ' ; ` \ * If required, click Add another to add multiple users: Review the user details, then click Add users to save the details. Bulk import user details (Excel upload method) Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the left, then click Bulk import Download the user details template file. Ensure the App User tab is selected. Click Download template to get an offline Excel file copy (Download begins automatically). Prepare the template file. Note : Maintain the original template structure to avoid any uploading errors. Note : You can add up to 10,000 users in a single file upload. Open the downloaded file. Enter user details ( User ID Name Team ) in their respective columns. ℹ️ Important A new team is created, and the user gets assigned if the entered Team name does not exist in the Workspace. ℹ️ Important: Ensure the entered User ID(s) meet the following criteria - The user ID must not exceed the 64-character limit. - Avoid using following characters: < > & " ' ; ` \ * Save the prepared file on your computer. Upload the prepared template copy. Return to the Sanas Portal, click Select Excel file and upload the prepared template file. Click Review upload to verify the uploaded user details. Upon review, Portal highlights errors if any of the entered user details are missing or do not meet the criteria. Rectify errors, if encountered. Review the error summary or select Download error report for a detailed error overview . Fix these errors on the prepared template file and re-upload it. You’ll see a successful review message if all the previously reported errors are resolved on the re-uploaded file. Click Download report to take a detailed overview of the final actions. Click Confirm upload to save the changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Move app users between teams
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Moving App User between teams is an essential admin task for managing app users on the Sanas Portal. The action becomes helpful in the following scenarios: Note : Inter Workspace movement of App users is not allowed. App activation mode : Due to the nature of specific app activation modes, like auto-activation, the app users get added to the Workspace’s default Team. You can use the move app user feature to map the app users to the correct teams. Internal transfers : Change the app users’ Teams if they are transferred internally to different projects. Change in shifts : Change the app users’ Teams if you run Teams based on Work shifts. This guide provides detailed instructions on moving app users between teams. You can move them in the following ways: Move via Portal UI : Move app users using the Sanas Portal UI. Move via bulk import : Move app users in bulk via a template upload. Before you begin Access : You’ll need access on the Sanas Portal to move app users. The following roles on the Sanas Portal can take action: Admin : Can move app users between any teams. Supervisor : Can move app users between the teams to which they are assigned as supervisors. Move app user (via Portal UI) Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Click Users on the navigation menu, and ensure that the App users tab is selected. Select the Team to which the app user is currently assigned. Select the check box next to the app user you want to move. Moving multiple users at once is possible. Click Move users Select the destination Team from the Move to list. Click Move Users to confirm. Move app users (via Bulk import) Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the left and ensure the App users tab is selected. Click Bulk Import Download the template copy. Click Download template . This downloads an offline template copy to your computer. Prepare the template file. Open the downloaded template copy. Enter the intended app users’ User IDs and Names in the respective columns. Enter the destination Team name for each user. ℹ️ Important : Ensure you enter the Team name correctly. If you enter a Team name that currently doesn’t exist in the Workspace, Sanas will creates a new Team with that name, and assign the app users to it. Save the prepared template file. Upload the template. Return to the Sanas Portal, click Select Excel file, and upload your prepared template file. Click Review upload Review actions. Errors: If you encounter upload errors, review the summary or click Download error report . Take the corrective actions accordingly and re-upload the file Success: Review the summary or click 'Download report' if the template uploads successfully Click Confirm upload to save the changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance. Users of the Sanas desktop application.

pages.title: Deactivate or reactivate the app user
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide explains how to deactivate an app user and how to reactivate a previously deactivated one. Before you begin Access : You’ll need access to the Sanas Portal to follow the procedure below. Limitation : The portal users can take the following actions: Admin : Deactivate or reactivate an app user from any Team within the Workspace. Supervisor : Deactivate or reactivate the app user from the assigned Teams only. Deactivate app user (via Portal UI) Note : Avoid manual app user deactivation with automatic deactivation for inactive app users . Automatic detactivation is currently limited to the Accent Translation Workspaces. Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu and ensure the App users tab is selected. Select the Team containing the users you want to deactivate. Select the check box next to the app user(s) you want to deactivate. Use the search bar to find app users in the selected team. Click Deactivate users. In the confirmation dialog box, click Deactivate to confirm your action. Review the deactivated app users to confirm the changes. See Review deactivated app users Deactivate app user (via Bulk import) Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu. Click Bulk import . Opens the bulk import window. Ensure the App users tab is selected. Click Download template Open the downloaded template and enter the following users’ details: Note : Enter Yes in the template’s deactivate column next to the user you wish to deactivate. You may encounter an error if the user details you entered are incorrect. Parameter Value User ID User ID of the app user Name Full name Team Currently assigned Team Deactivate Yes Click Select Excel file to browse and upload the prepared template file from your computer. Click Review upload to analyze the action. If you encounter an error, review the details or click Download error report for detailed analysis. Modify the template file accordingly and re-upload it. If the template uploads successfully, review the actions or click Download report for a detailed analysis. Click Confirm upload to save changes. Reactivate the app user Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu. Ensure the App users tab is selected. Click View deactivated users under the ellipsis ( ) menu option. Select the check box next to the app user(s) you want to reactivate. Click Activate Click Activate to confirm your action. Reactivated app users are reassigned to the Team they were assigned to before deactivation. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance. A Team is a unit within a Sanas Workspace that groups App Users working on a common project.

pages.title: Invite Admin or Supervisors on Sanas Portal
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide provides instructions on how to invite Portal Users (Admins or Supervisors). You can invite them via: Email invite : Sends email invite to the intended users. Sign-up link : Share sign-up links through your preferred communication channel. Bulk Import : Import users’ details by uploading a template file. Before you begin You must have admin access to the Sanas Portal to invite other Portal users. The invited admins get verified with their work email addresses Invite by email Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu, then select the Portal Users tab. Click Add Users . Opens the Add users window. Select a role between Admin and Supervisor from the drop-down menu. The selected role is assigned to all the invited users. Enter the work email addresses to send the invites. You can invite up to 10 users per request. Add emails separated by a comma (,). Ensure that you have added all intended emails correctly. Click Add Users to send invitations. Refer to the Accept Invitation guide for detailed instructions for the Sanas Portal sign-up. Invite by sign-up link Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu, then select the Portal Users tab. Click Add Users . Opens the Add users window. Select a role between Admin and Supervisor from the drop-down menu. The selected role gets assigned to all the invited users. Click Copy link . This is the common sign-up link for all Portal users you wish to invite. Note The invitation link doesn't expire with time. Ensure you share the link with only the intended users. Share the sign-up link with the intended users through your preferred communication platform. Refer to the Accept Invitation guide for detailed instructions for the Sanas Portal sign-up. Bulk import Portal user details Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Click Users from the navigation menu, then select the Portal Users tab. Click Bulk import . Opens the bulk import window. Click Download template to save an offline copy. Select a role between Admin and Supervisor from the drop-down menu. The selected role is assigned to all the invited users. Enter the following users’ details to prepare the template file: ℹ️ Important - Bulk import limits 50 users' details per request. - Maintain the original template structure to avoid upload errors. Parameter Details Email Enter the work email addresses of the invited users Name The invited users’ full names Teams (Only if the Supervisor role is selected) Enter the Team name you wish to assign to the user. ℹ️ Important : If the entered team does not exist, Sanas will create a new team with that name and assign the user to it. Deactivate To deactivate an existing Portal admin, enter 'Yes' in the column next to the user. Sanas takes the following actions by default if the entered Admin Supervisor details already exist on the Workspace. Update : The Admin/Supervisor details get updated as defined in the template. Deactivate : The Admin/Supervisor gets deactivated if the Deactivation column has the “Yes” entry. Come back to the Bulk import window, and click Select Excel file . Browse and select the prepared template copy from your computer. Click Review upload If you encounter an error, review the details or click Download error report for a detailed analysis. Fix the errors accordingly and re-upload it. If the template uploads successfully, review the action details or click Download report for detailed analysis. Finally, click Confirm upload to save the changes. Refer to the Accept Invitation guide for detailed instructions for the Sanas Portal sign-up. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Automatic deactivation for inactive app users
pages.text: summary Prev Next About The following guide explains how to configure the automatic deactivation of inactive app users. Note : The feature is currently limited to the Accent Translation workspaces only What is Automatic Deactivation? Automatic deactivation is an app user management feature that eliminates the need for manual deactivation for inactive app users. The feature, upon configuration in a Workspace, automatically deactivates app users once no app activity is recorded against the user for a defined period. How does auto-deactivation work? Auto-deactivation configuration : The admin user configures auto-deactivation for inactive app users on a Workspace and defines the inactivity period. Active users : The app user is considered active until the system records at least one app activation during the period. Inactivity measurement : The inactivity period of a user is measured from the timestamp of their last recorded app logout. Reactivation: Auto-deactivated app users can be easily reactivated at any time. Before You Begin Ensure you are assigned with the Admin role on the Sanas Portal to modify the configuration. Procedure Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Navigate to the Settings page, then scroll down to the Deactivate Inactive App Users section. Enable the Deactivate Inactive App Users option and define the inactivity duration. Click Save to apply the changes. Once deactivated, the app users gets moved to the Deactivated users page. FAQs How is user inactivity determined? Answer : Inactivity is calculated based on the last time the user used the Sanas app. Can I re-activate deactivated users? Answer : Yes, deactivated users (whether automatically or manually) can be re-activated. For instructions, refer to the guide on re-activating app users Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Enable Sanas Personalization
pages.text: summary Prev Next This guide explains the Sanas Personalization feature and how to enable it for a Workspace from the Sanas Portal. Sanas Personalization Sanas' Personalization feature enables Sanas app users to create and use a voice profile that is optimized for their voice and enhances their accent-translated voice by preserving their natural voice identity, enhancing overall naturalness, and making it more human. Key points Data security & safety - No audio gets recorded or stored anywhere. Feature availability : The Sanas Personalization feature is available on the Sanas app version 4.3.X and above. User status : Admins can review the Personalization status (Completed or Not completed) for each user on the Users page. Voice profiling : During voice profile creation, app users need to read aloud a short sentence. If needed, they can recreate the profile at any time through the app. Enable Sanas Personalization Follow the steps below to enable Sanas Personalization for a Workspace: Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. If you’ve multiple Workspaces, navigate to the Workspace you wish to enable this feature using the Workspace Switcher at the top-left corner. Workspace Switcher Click Settings on the left-side navigation menu, and scroll down to the Sanas Personalization section under the App Configurations. Enable the Sanas Personalization and confirm your action. Once enabled, users on the supported Sanas app versions ( 4.3.X and above) will see the Sanas Personalization option available on their app. Refer to the Create voice profile guide for detailed instructions for the app user. Review User Status for Sanas Personalization Do the following to review users’ status: Navigate to your desired Workspace and click Users from the left-side navigation menu. Select the team you wish to review. You can review the Sanas Personalization status for each user. You’ll find the following statuses: Completed - User has created a voice profile Not completed - Voice profile creation is pending Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Automatic Volume Optimization
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Automatic Volume Optimization AVO ) automatically adjusts your softphone's headset volume when audio distortion or sudden volume spikes are detected. This ensures call recipients experience smooth, consistent audio quality throughout the conversation. Once enabled at the workspace level, the feature operates silently in the background—no action required from app users. Prerequisites Before enabling AVO, ensure you have: Admin access to the Sanas Portal Sanas app version 4.1.X or higher is deployed to users. Guide: Enable AVO for a Workspace Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Select the desired workspace. Navigate to Settings and scroll to the Automatic Volume Optimization section. Toggle the feature on and confirm. Once enabled, AVO activates automatically for all users on supported app versions (4.1.X+). Users on older app versions will continue using the Sanas app without AVO functionality. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.
