Disable Sanas for Team Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Navigate to the Users page. Click the option menu ( ) next to the team you want to act on , then click Disable Sanas for all The team users will no longer be able to use Sanas. Disable Sanas for the user Follow Steps 1 to 3 of Disable Sanas for Team Select the team where the user is assigned. Click the option menu ( ) next to the user you want to act on , then click Disable Sanas Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Enabling Sanas Widget
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This article explains Sanas Widget and how to enable it for an Accent Translation AT ) Workspace from the Sanas Portal. What is Sanas Widget? The Sanas Widget is an essential feature for the app users who need to turn off Sanas quickly during a call. This feature becomes handy in scenarios where the app user needs to speak in another language (other than English) and wants to take a quick action. Sanas Widgets provides a quick toggle functionality for Sanas users who often need to switch between multiple languages during a live call. The current flow of disabling Sanas from the app requires you to open the app and disable the Sanas after selecting an appropriate reason, which creates significant friction when working with a live call. Key features Quick toggle: The widget features a toggle that indicates the current Sanas Status, enabling users to switch between On and Off states without opening the whole app. Always available : Once enabled from the Portal, the widget remains on the user's screen even when the whole app is minimized, making it easy to access. No reason selection needed : Users can disable Sanas without selecting a reason, streamlining the process. Supervisors will still receive notifications about Before you begin The Sanas Widget is only supported for users running the Sanas app version [ 4.0.X and above ]. Ensure all app users in the workspace are running the supported app version. Users with older app versions won’t see the widget feature even if it is enabled for their workspace. Available only on the AT workspaces. Enabling widget for a workspace Log in to the Sanas Portal by using your credentials. You’ll need the Admin privilege on the Sanas Portal to modify app configuration for a workspace. Navigate to the Settings page and scroll down to the Show Widget option under the App configurations. Toggle on the widget option, then click Save to apply the changes. Using the widget feature Launch the Sanas app and activate it with your credentials, if applicable. Minimize the Sanas app. You’ll see a Sanas widget on your screen with a toggle button to turn Sanas on or off. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure SSO for Sanas Portal
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Single Sign-On (SSO) is a quick and easy way to authenticate and provides a seamless experience for the Portal Users. This guide provides instructions to configure SSO for the Sanas Portal. Prerequisites Access Requirements — Administrator privileges on the Portal and the Identity Provider (IdP) to perform configuration. User Invitation — For SSO to work, ensure all Portal Users are already added to their relevant Workspaces. Refer to Add Portal Users for instructions. Note: Users attempting to authenticate through SSO who aren’t part of any Workspace will fail authentication. Configure Portal SSO Follow the procedure below to configure SSO on the Sanas Portal: Enable SSO on Portal Get SSO Configuration Details from Portal Log in to the Sanas Portal with your admin credentials. Navigate to the Settings menu. Click Manage under the Portal Authentication. Enable the SSO option if it’s disabled, and copy the following: Identifier Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL) In the next step, Prepare SSO configuration on the IdP provider As a next step, you’ll create a SAML application with your preferred IdP provider. In general, the SSO configuration steps remain common for any IdP provider. For the demonstration, we’ll configure SSO using Okta. Create a SAML Application in Okta. Log in to your Okta account In Okta, navigate to Applications > Applications and click Create App Integration Select SAML 2.0 as the sign-in method, then click Next Enter the following application details, then click Next Note : Application details (app name and logo) will be visible for the Portal Users. App Name : Enter an app name (e.g., "Sanas Portal"). (Optional) App Logo : Upload a logo. Configure the SAML settings: Single Sign-On URL : Enter the Reply URL you copied from the Portal. Audience URI : Enter the Identifier you copied from the Portal. Name ID Format : Set to EmailAddress Application Username : Set to Okta username Note: Name ID Format and Application Username attributes are mandatory and must be set to email address and Okta username of the users. Portal validates users using these attributes. Under Attribute Statements , configure the following mappings: username user.login name user.firstName + " " + user.lastName (Optional) sanasTeam user.sanasTeam sanasUserType user.sanasUserType Select the checkbox, then click Finish Copy Sign On Details from Okta Open the created application on Okta. Navigate to the Sign On tab and copy the Sign On URL From the SAML Signing Certificates section, download the certificate (SHA-2 > Action > Download certificate). Use the below IdP resources for SSO configurations: Azure AD Google Save the SSO configuration on the Portal Return to the SSO configuration window on the Portal. Enter the Sign on URL Upload the X.509 certificate you’ve downloaded from Okta. Click Save to apply the changes. Perform a test authentication on the Portal using the configured SSO Okta. Troubleshooting Ensure the SSO is configured correctly for the following points: User present on IdP — Ensure all the intended Portal users are already present on the IdP provider you’ve configured for SSO. Attributes mapping — Ensure the following user attributes are configured during SSO configuration on IdP: email — email added on Portal name — name added on Portal. Sign On URL — Ensure the correct Sign On URL is configured on the Portal. The portal uses this URL to authorize the user’s access. Certificate Upload — Ensure the correct certificate is uploaded on Portal. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure app activation mode
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction The app activation Mode is the app license activation mechanism for the users before they start using the Sanas app. Activation mode allows effective user and license management and assists Portal users in reviewing app utilization among users. What are the available activation modes? Below are the available activation modes: User Activation Key UAK ): UAK is a credential-based activation method that requires the user’s User ID and Workspace ID for activation. Portal users must manually add the app users' details and share these credentials with the intended app users to allow them to access the app. Auto-activation : Auto-activation is a domain-synced activation method that utilizes the computer’s connected domain and logged-in user profile details for app activation. If auto-activation is configured, the app activates automatically once the user launches the app on their computer, provided the user’s computer is connected to the organization's domain and the user is logged in to the computer with their user profile. Default app activation modes If no customization is done, app users will find the activation modes below for their Sanas apps. - Accent Translation app: UAK - Noise Cancellation app: Auto- activation Configure app activation mode Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Settings from the left-side navigation. Scroll down to the App activation mode section. You can see the currently activated activation mode. Select your desired activation mode, and click Save to apply the changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Auto activation mode
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview Auto activation is an app activation mode that allows users to activate their app without manually entering their credentials before they start using it. Auto-activation validates the user’s identity using the connected domain, such as Azure AD, on their computer and their user profile details. Upon validation, an active app license gets assigned to the user. For detailed instructions on activating the Sanas app with auto activation, refer to the user guides for Accent Translation or Noise Cancellation Benefits of using auto activation mode Credential-Free Activation: Users can activate Sanas apps without manually entering login credentials, creating a seamless onboarding experience. Automated User Provisioning: User details are automatically added to the default Team within your Workspace during the first activation, eliminating the need for manual user management and credential sharing for administrators. Pre-Configuration Requirements Before enabling auto-activation, review these important considerations: User Team Assignment: Users activated through auto-activation are initially assigned to the default team in your Workspace. Administrators can reassign users to appropriate teams after activation if needed. Workspace Compatibility : Auto-activation can only be configured for Workspaces without existing license assignments. Attempting to configure auto-activation on incompatible Workspaces will result in an error message. Workaround for Incompatible Workspaces Create a new Workspace and migrate your teams to enable auto-activation functionality. Contact Sanas Support if you need any assistance with creating new Workspace. Default Activation Modes by Workspace Type: Noise Cancellation Workspaces: Auto-activation Accent Translation Workspaces: User Activation Key (UAK) Configuration Steps Prerequisites: You’ll need admin access on the Sanas Portal to modify the app activation mode. Navigate to the Sanas Portal and log in using your credentials. Click Settings from the main navigation menu and scroll to the App activation mode section. Select Auto-activation from the available options (if not currently selected). Click Save to apply your changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure Workspace Time Zone
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide walks you through the steps to configure time zone settings for a Workspace in the Sanas Portal What is Workspace's specific timezone? Workspace-specific time zone configuration allows Portal admins to define a unified time zone for a given Workspace. Once set, the timestamp across Sanas Reports will align with this selected time zone, regardless of the Sanas Portal user’s local device time zone. If no time zone is configured, the Portal defaults to using the user's browser-based time zone. Prerequisites You’ll need the Admin privilege on the Sanas Portal to configure the Timezone. Configure Timezone Note : Time zone settings apply only to the currently selected Workspace. Other workspaces will continue to use the default ( browser-based ) mode unless configured separately. Navigate to the Sanas Portal and log in using your credentials. Select your desired Workspace from the Workspace Switcher at the top-left corner. Click Settings from the main navigation menu and scroll to the Time Zone section. Choose your preferred time zone mode: Browser-based : Displays timestamps based on each user’s local device time zone. Workspace-based : Allows the selection of a specific timezone. All timestamps will be set to the selected timezone for all Portal users. If selected Workspace based timezone, choose your desired timezone from the drop-down menu. Click Save to apply the changes. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance. The Workspace Switcher is a navigation feature that allows users to switch between multiple Workspaces within a Sanas account seamlessly.

pages.title: Configure Noise Cancellation with Omni-Directional Capabilities
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide explains the noise cancellation with the Omni Directional capabilities feature on the Sanas Noise Cancellation NC ) app and provides a procedure for configuring it from the Sanas Portal. Feature availability : The omni directional noise cancellation feature is available in the Sanas NC app version 3.2.17 and above. Ensure your Sanas NC app is running the latest available version. What is Omni Directional Noise Cancellation? Omni Directional noise cancellation utilizes our advanced speech understanding AI models, which eliminate noises from your and recipients’ voices (Omni Directional) in real time, ensuring the best calling clarity and experience for everyone you call. Benefits of using Omni directional noise cancellation: Clear communication (outbound calls): Your voice sounds clearer, irrespective of your environment or background. Our AI models process your voice and eliminate any background noise your microphone captures. Better understanding (inbound calls): Understand your recipient's voice clearly, irrespective of their environment or background. The AI model clarifies the recipient's voice before it reaches your ears, without any action needed from the recipient's side. No additional commitments : The Omni directional Noise Cancellation capability is embedded in the latest Sanas NC app versions ( 3.2.17 and above) and requires no extra hardware to deploy. Before you begin You’ll need admin access to the Sanas Portal to perform the configuration below. Ensure all your app users in the Workspace use the latest available Sanas NC app version . App users with incompatible Sanas NC app versions won't see the Omni Directional features on their apps. Configure Omni Directional Noise Cancellation Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Settings from the navigation menu and scroll to the App configuration section. Select the “ Allow noise cancellation for outgoing and incoming audio ” option to enable the omnidirectional noise cancellation feature. Note : The feature gets enabled at the Workspace level and will be available for all users running the compatible Sanas NC app versions. App users need to start a new app session to reflect the features of their app. Refer to the Using Sanas Noise Cancellation app guide for app users’ instructions. (Optional) Enforce the app configurations for all app users if required. Doing this will disallow the app users to disable the Sanas Noise Cancellation manually from their app, hence allowing you to align with the organization's policies. Select Disallow users to Enable/Disable Noise Cancellation You can still disable Noise Cancellation for specific app users or Teams in the enforcement-enabled Workspace from the Sanas Portal for any exceptions. Click Save to apply the changes made to the app configurations. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Enforce Sanas synthesis for all app users
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Enforcing Sanas synthesis for all app users in a Sanas Workspace removes the ability to disable Sanas synthesis manually from the Sanas app for the app users. Admins can ensure that all app users in a Sanas Workspace have Sanas enabled all the time during an active app session, aligning with their organization’s policies and providing the best calling experience all the time. Upon configuration, the app users can no longer see the Sanas toggle. If required, Admin can still disable Sasas for Team and Individual app users if Sanas synthesis is enforced at the Workspace level. This guide provides instructions on configuring the app from the Sanas Portal. Feature availability By default, Sanas synthesis isn’t enforced on any Workspace but can be configured by the Admin. To configure this feature, ensure the deployed Sanas apps are on the below app versions: Accent Translation App version 2.24.1205.9 and above Noise Cancellation : App version v2.24.1205.8 and above Before you begin You’ll need the admin role privileges on the Sanas Portal to modify Sanas app configurations. Configuration steps The synthesis enforcement procedure is common for the Sanas NC and AT apps. The steps below demonstrate the steps for the Sanas AT app, but the same could be followed for the NC app. ℹ️ Important : Upon the synthesis enforcement, the Sanas app gets enabled for any user who has manually disabled it in a current active ongoing session. Users will not be able to manually turn it off from the app. However, in this scenario, the Admin can manually disable Sanas for an entire Team in the Workspace or Individual use r if required. Navigate to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Click Settings from the left-side navigation. Scroll down to the User Preference section, and select the Disallow users to Enable/ Disable Accent Translation option. Note : For Sanas NC, you’ll see the Disallow users to Enable/ Disable Noise Cancellation Click Save to apply the changes. Disable Sanas for a Team Disabling Sanas for an entire team is possible only if the Sanas synthesis is enforced for its parent Workspace. Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials, and navigate to your desired Workspace. Click Users from the left-side navigation, and ensure you are on the App users tab. Click the ellipsis ( ) menu button next to the Team you wish to act on, then click Disable Sanas for all Repeat the above steps if you wish to re-enable Sanas for the Team. Disable Sanas for an individual user Disabling Sanas for an individual app user is possible only if the Sasnas synthesis is enforced in their current Workspace. Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials, and navigate to your desired Workspace. Click Users from the left-side navigation, and ensure you are on the App users tab. Select the Team to which the app user is currently added. Click the ellipsis ( ) menu button next to the app user for whom you wish to disable Sanas, then click Disable Sanas Repeat the above steps to re-enable Sanas for the app user. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Manage Incompatible Setup Warning
pages.text: summary Prev Next About This guide provides instructions for managing notifications related to setup incompatibility for Sanas app users. Why it’s important? The feature is specifically handy in cases when you don’t wish to show these error messages at your app user’s application and would want to manage these at the backend. Additionally, it helps facilitate timely app audits on the app users’ devices done by your customers to avoid unnecessary escalations. Before you begin You must have administrator privileges on the Sanas Portal to modify configurations. Procedure Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials or Single Sign-On SSO ) options. Navigate to the Settings page, and scroll down to the Incompatible Setup Warning section Select one of the following options to configure the notification behavior: Info: Incompatible warnings are hidden only for app users. Hiding warning messages only prevents them from being displayed to app users. All detected setup incompatibility warnings will still be captured in the Sanas Portal and highlighted for administrators and supervisors. Show warning to app users – Displays setup incompatibility warnings to Sanas app users. Don’t show warning to app users – Hides warning messages from Sanas app users. From the pop-up message window, click Confirm to save your changes. FAQs Where are these warnings captured or notified? Answer : All setup incompatibility warnings are logged in the Sanas Portal . Administrators and supervisors will see these warnings next to the affected app user, allowing them to take necessary actions. What should users do if they encounter a warning when notifications are disabled? Answer : Users will not be notified about setup incompatibility warnings and can continue using the Sanas app without interruption. The relevant administrator or supervisor will contact the user directly if any action is required. Support Need help? Get in touch with our support team or raise a support ticket.

pages.title: Reset password for Sanas Portal
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide provides instructions on how to reset your Sanas Portal password. You can reset the password from: Login page : Reset password right from the Sanas Portal login page. Profile : Reset password from your Portal profile. Reset password from the login page Navigate to the Sanas Portal page from your preferred web browser. Open the received email, and click Reset password . Opens the password reset page. Configure your new password for Sanas Portal, then click Reset password Reset password from the profile Log in to the Sanas Portal with your existing password. Click on your profile icon in the top-right corner, then click Profile Click Change password Configure your new password, then click Change Support Need help? pages.title: Configure Auto Update
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide explains how the Auto Update feature works and provides step-by-step instructions for configuring it through the Sanas Portal The Sanas app's auto update feature allows admins to roll out updates in a controlled manner, ensuring no downtime due to the update. Benefits of Auto Update Compared to manual updates, the auto update feature offers the following benefits: Custom time slot : Configure specific time slots for when users receive update notifications. Throttle bandwidth : Throttle bandwidth during update downloads to minimize disruption. Assisted app update: Once an update is released, app users are notified within the specified time slot. They can update immediately or defer the update to a more convenient time. How auto update works The auto update feature consists of three main stages: Configuration: Admins set up the update timeslot and, optionally, configure bandwidth throttling through the Sanas Portal. User Update: Users are notified of the update during the specified timeslot and can choose when to install it. Before you begin Ensure that you: Have admin access to the Sanas Portal. Understand that once auto update is configured, it cannot be rolled back . Contact Sanas Support if you need any assistance. Configure auto update Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. From the left-hand menu, go to Settings and scroll to the Auto Updates section. Click Manage Set your desired Start and End times for when users should receive update notifications. Note : Times are based on the user's local timezone. (Optional) Check the box labeled “Would you like to configure...” to enable bandwidth throttling. If throttling is enabled, select a download speed from the dropdown. This will be the maximum download speed for app updates. Click Save to apply your configuration. Roll Out App Updates From the Sanas Portal, click Download App from the left-side navigation. Click View in the notification to go to the Download App page. Click Start Update to roll out the new version to all eligible users (users with a minimum app version of v3) in the Workspace. ⚠️ Important : If needed, you can click Stop Update to cancel the ongoing rollout. However, users who have already updated will not be rolled back. Monitor the Update You’ll be able to see the following: Update Status: Update in Progress Update Completed Latest App Version: Displays the new version being deployed. Users Eligible for Auto Update: Lists users whose app version meets the minimum requirement. Others will need to update manually. Users Updated to Latest Version: Tracks users who have completed the update. For app update instructions, refer to the app update guide. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Enable Inbound Noise Cancellation for Accent Translation Users
pages.text: summary Prev Next This guide provides instructions to enable the Inbound Noise Cancellation NC ) feature for the Accent Translation AT ) users from the Sanas Portal. The Inbound Noise Cancellation features require a minimum Sanas app version of 4.2.X or above. Inbound and Outbound NC Inbound NC eliminates the background noises from the recipient’s voice, ensuring the Sanas app user hears the recipient loud and clear, irrespective of their background environment. Similarly, the Outbound NC is intended for the recipients, and it eliminates any background noise from the Sanas app user’s voice before it reaches the recipient. The combination of Inbound and Outbound NC creates a true noise-free calling experience for both individuals on the call, helping to reduce any misunderstanding due to the background noise. Before you begin; You must have the admin role access on the Sanas Portal to update the app configuration for a Workspace. Minimum app version 4.2.X or higher for all app users in the workspace Users on older versions won't see the Inbound NC controls on their app post feature enablement from the Portal, but can continue using other available features. Enable Inbound Noise Cancellation Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials, and ensure you are in your desired Workspace. Use the Workspace Switcher at the top-left corner of the Portal to navigate between workspaces. Navigate to the workspace settings page, and scroll to the Accent Translation with Inbound Noise Cancellation capabilities section. Select Allow Accent Translation for outgoing audio and Noise Cancellation for incoming audio to configure the Inbound NC for AT users. Inbound Noise Cancellation with Accent Translation Click Save to apply the changes. What next? Once the feature is enabled, app users must end any ongoing session and restart their app to see the Inbound NC controls on their app. By default, the Inbound NC toggle is turned on. App users can manually disable the Inbound NC toggle at any time they need, based on their requirements. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Recommended audio settings
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Sanas needs constant access to your system’s audio for its operations. As Sanas is supported on multiple platforms, it becomes essential to follow specific recommended audio settings based on the type of conferencing or softphone service you use. This guide provides generic audio settings recommendations for your system. Recommended audio settings Follow the audio settings based on the type of your softphone: ℹ️ Note : The following configuration is tested on the Sanas app versions 2.24.0731 and above. Browser-based services The browser-based softphone services, by default, pick the audio settings configured at the system level. Update the audio settings at the system level by selecting Sanas Microphone or Sanas Virtual Audio under the Audio input options. Ensure you save and apply the configuration, and refresh the softphone service if it’s already launched. Application-based services Update your application’s audio settings by following the steps below: Navigate to the application’s audio settings. Under the audio inputs section, select Sanas Microphone or Sanas Virtual Audio. Save or apply the configuration. Make sure you refresh the application before making an actual call. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Configure accents for a Workspace
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview This guide explains how to update source and target accents for your workspace. When you change accent settings, Sanas automatically selects the optimal AI model and deploys it to your users seamlessly. Note : We recommend avoiding frequent changes to workspace accents, as they trigger the AI model to update for all app users in the Workspace. How accent changes work When you AI modify accent configuration, here's what happens: Automatic AI model selection - Sanas analyzes your new accent pairing and updates the AI model if required. Seamless background update During the download Users continue working with their current model. Only the accent translation becomes temporarily unavailable during the update period if the new configured accent requires a different AI model New AI model downloads silently in the background No service interruption or forced restarts. After the download completes App automatically switches to the new AI model seamlessly Full accent translation capability restored No user action required. Before you begin Verify app version compatibility - Only users on Sanas app version 4.4.X or higher receive automatic AI model updates. Users on older versions Continue using their current AI model Retain existing accent translation capabilities Receive AI model update after upgrading to v4.4.X+ Recommendation : Update users to the latest version before changing accents to ensure a consistent experience. Configure Accents Step 1: Access workspace settings Log in to Sanas Portal Navigate to your target workspace. Click Settings from the left navigation panel Step 2: Locate accent translation settings Scroll to the Accent Translation section. Step 3: Select accents Choose your source and target accents from the dropdown menus: Source Accent (User's regional accent) Target Accent (Recipient hears) India (IND) United States (US) Philippines (PHI) United Kingdom (UK) Latin America (LATAM) Africa Middle East (AFRME) Example : If your team members speak with Indian accents and primarily serve US customers, select: Source accent : India (IND) Target accent : United States (US) Step 4: Save Changes Your selections save automatically. The system immediately begins evaluating AI model requirements and initiating updates for compatible users. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Override default AI models
pages.text: summary Prev Next Overview This guide shows you how to manually select AI models for your workspace, overriding Sanas-recommended defaults. About our recommendations : Sanas recommends AI models based on your workspace's configured accents, informed by internal testing and customer feedback. While we optimize for performance and reliability, you can choose any available model to meet specific requirements. Before You Begin Check app version compatibility- Model updates only reach users on the Sanas app version 4.4.X or higher. Users on older versions continue using their current model until they upgrade Action needed : Update users to the latest app version to enable model switchability. Verify auto-update configuration - Model updates deploy according to your configured update preferences. Ensure auto-update is properly configured before proceeding. Setup guide Configure App Auto-Update Select a Different AI Model Step 1: Access the Download App Page Log in to Sanas Portal with your credentials. Click Download App in the left navigation panel. Step 2: Initiate Model Selection Click Start Update to begin the model selection process. Step 3: Choose Models Select your preferred AI model from the dropdown menu for each Sanas capability: Step 4: Deploy the Update Click Start Auto Update after making your selections. Users on compatible app versions ( v4.4.X+ ) receive an update notification. Users proceed with the update based on their configured preferences. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Lock Voice Profile Selection
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction Voice profiles are essential to delivering accurate accent translation and maintaining a natural, engaging conversational tone. The Lock Voice Profile feature allows administrators to enforce a specific voice profile for Accent Translation (AT) users, ensuring consistency across their organization's Sanas usage. Lock Profile Selection Lock Voice Profile Selection is an administrative feature available for AT workspaces. When enabled, it ensures that users are assigned and locked to a specific voice profile within the Sanas app. Upon enabling the feature, users running a supported app version ( 4.6.x or above) will be prompted to select a voice profile the next time they launch the app. Once a profile is selected and saved, it is tagged to the user's account and cannot be changed from the app interface. Administrators can review and update voice profile selections for users at any time through the Portal. Admin setup Prerequisites Minimum required app version : Lock Voice Profile Selection is supported on Sanas app version 4.6.x and above. Users running an older version will not be affected by the feature, even if it has been enabled in the workspace. Ensure all users in the workspace are running a compatible version before proceeding. Administrator access: You must have Administrator-level access to the Portal to enable this feature. Enabling Lock Voice Profile Selection Log in to the Portal Navigate to Settings > Lock Voice Profile Selection Toggle On the setting. Reviewing or Updating a User's Voice Profile To review or update the voice profile assigned to an AT user, follow the steps below: Navigate to the Sanas Portal and ensure the correct workspace is selected in the top-left corner. Click Users , then open the App Users tab and select the team the user belongs to. Locate the user in the list. Their current voice profile is displayed under the Voice column. To update the profile, click the action button ( ) next to the user and select Change User Profile Select the preferred voice profile, then click Save User setup Selecting a Voice Profile (First-Time Setup) Launch the Sanas app on your computer and activate it. A voice profile selection prompt will appear automatically. Select your preferred voice profile and click Update Now Your selected profile will be applied immediately. If you need to change your voice profile in the future, please contact your administrator to submit a change request. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Schedule Reports
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide provides step-by-step instructions to schedule the Sanas Report. Scheduled reports are automatically generated at regular intervals and delivered to specified recipients via email in Excel format. Before you begin You’ll need access to the Sanas Portal to create a report schedule. Create a report schedule Log in to the Sanas Portal using your credentials. Navigate to the Reports page. Click Schedule , then click + New Schedule Note : All report data aligns with your workspace's timezone. You can verify a workspace’s timezone on both the Home and Reports pages. Select your report delivery frequency from one of the following options: Frequency Description Data included Hourly Choose an interval (eg, every 3 hours). The current day’s data. For example, if the interval is set to 3 hours. The first report is delivered at 03:00 with the first three hours of data, and subsequent reports will be sent at 06:00 with the next six hours of data for the current day. Daily Select a specific time for delivery. The previous day's complete data Weekly Choose a day and time for delivery. The previous week's complete data. Monthly Select a date and time for delivery. The previous month's complete data. Use the search function to find and select the scheduled report’s recipients. Add multiple recipients as per requirement. Important : If you can't find someone in the recipient list, verify that they are added to the Sanas Portal with admin or supervisor permissions. Finally, click Schedule report to save your configuration. Sanas will now schedule your report delivery based on the above configuration. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Understand Sanas Reports
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction The Report page serves as your centralized analytics console for monitoring and analyzing Sanas app usage across teams within a Workspace. It consolidates key metrics to help you gain insights and make data-driven decisions. Report summary The report summary is the header of your Report page, highlighting the following key metrics: Metric Description New users New app users created within the selected Workspace during the selected period. Active users App users that activated the Sanas app in the selected period. Example : The app user launches and activates the Sanas app on their computer (need not to engage the microphone or make a call). Sanas disabled App users with Sanas toggled off on their app. Click Sanas Disabled to review the metric for individual app user. Example : App user launches and activates the Sanas app, then manually it turn off. Incompatible setups App users encountered system compatibility errors during the selected period. Click Incompatible setups to review the metric for individual app user. Example : Incompatibility error occurs when user disconnect their headset during an active session. Utilization table The Analytics table offers a detailed overview of each individual app user within the selected team (default: All teams) for the specified time period (default: Today). It includes the following metrics: Metric Description User ID Unique identifier Name Full name Team Currently assigned team Machine Computer unique identifier Login Timestamp of the first Sanas app interaction. Example : User logged in to the Sanas app at the beginning of their work shift. Last seen Timestamp of the last Sanas app activity. Example A user logs out, or an inactivity period is detected. Session The total active time between the Login and Last seen is calculated as the Session duration. The Session duration excludes any inactivity period longer than 3 hours. Example : If a user logs in at 10:00 AM, becomes inactive from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, and resumes activity, the 4-hour inactivity period will be excluded from the session duration. App enabled The total time users have the Sanas app activated with the Sanas toggle turned on. Periods of inactivity—such as app logout, screen lock, or device sleep—are excluded from the total duration. Status A user's engagement status is displayed as either Engaged or Not Engaged based on their usage during a selected session. Engaged - The Sanas app was activated and used in at least one call during the selected session. Not Engaged - The Sanas app was activated but not used in any calls during the selected session. Usage Consolidation - If a user accesses the app from multiple devices within the same day (12:00 AM to 11:59 PM), their total usage duration is automatically consolidated into a single daily entry . This ensures accurate reporting per user per day, regardless of the number of devices used. Important considerations Please consider the following scenarios to understand the data reporting: Scenario Description Timezone differences The data displayed is based on the timezone of the admin user viewing the report. If two admins in different timezones view the same Workspace data for the same date range, slight variations may occur due to differences in their local time settings. Daily activity tracking App usage data is captured on a daily basis (from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM). A new entry is generated each day, aligned with this time window. Logins on multiple devices If a Sanas app user activates and uses their app through multiple devices in a single day (from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM), all the detected unique instances (machine + user credentials) of app usage get consolidated into a single line item on the Sanas Report. Customize reports You can tailor your reports using the following filters: Time Period Select a time range to view data for: Today ( default Yesterday Last 7 days Last 30 days Teams Choose specific teams in your Workspace to filter the report. By default, all teams are included. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Download reports

To learn more about report metrics and their use cases, see Understand Sanas Reports Before You Begin You must have Sanas Portal access to complete the steps below. Download Sanas Reports Follow the steps below to downalod Sanas Reports: Log in to the Sanas Portal with your credentials. Click Reports in the navigation menu. Click Download to save a copy of the report. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Generic audio configuration for web browsers

pages.title: Configure Amazon Connect (AWS Connect)

Connect your headset and select your headset’s microphone under the audio input menu on the Sanas app. Configure AWS Connect Navigate to AWS Connect on your preferred web browser and log in if required. pages.title: Configure Genesys Cloud CX Audio Configuration
pages.text: summary Prev Next This guide provides instructions to configure the audio source on the Genesys Cloud CX. The guide has dedicated audio configuration sections for omnidirectional and unidirectional communication types. Difference between omnidirectional and unidirectional communication: Omnidirectional communication : Applicable for the Sanas users using features like Omnidirectional Noise Cancellation (2-way Noise Cancellation), Inbound Noise Cancellation, etc. Unidirectional communication : Applicable for the Sanas users using one-way noise cancellation or accent translation. Decide your communication type based on the features configured on your Sanas app. Before you begin; Ensure you have the Sanas application installed on your computer. Make sure you have the required permissions to update the audio configurations on your Genesys Cloud softphone. Audio configuration Follow the applicable procedure based on the user preference configured on Sanas: Omnidirectional Communication Navigate to the Genesys Cloud CX application. Click on the profile icon at the top-left corner, then click Preferences Audio preferneces Click Sound under preferences, then choose one of the following options: Use Computer settings (recommended) - If selected, the default system audio preferences are applied to the Genesys Cloud CX application. New profile - Create your own custom audio profile and set it as the default. Note : Avoid creating multiple audio profiles as it may lead to confusion and possible disruption in usage. If creating a new profile, do the following: Expand the Use Computer settings , then click New Profile Create a new custom audio profile Enter the following profile details: Profile name - Enter a distinct name for the audio profile Microphone - Select Sanas Virtual Audio Speaker - Select Sanas Virtual Audio Ringer - Select your connected headset Click Save Audio profile - Configuration Ensure your created profile is selected. Expand the Advanced Mic Settings , and disable the following options: Automatic Mic Gain Off Disable Echo Cancellation Off Disable Noise Suppression Off Disable Disable the advanced in-built voice enhancement features Unidirectional Communication Navigate to the Genesys Cloud CX application. Click on the profile icon at the top-left corner, then click Preferences Audio preferneces Click Sound under preferences, then choose one of the following options: Use Computer settings (recommended) - If selected, the default system audio preferences are applied to the Genesys Cloud CX application. New profile - Create your own custom audio profile and set it as the default. Note : Avoid creating multiple audio profiles as it may lead to confusion and possible disruption in usage. If creating a new profile, do the following: Expand the Use Computer settings , then click New Profile Create a new custom audio profile Enter the following profile details: Profile name - Enter a distinct name for the audio profile Microphone - Select Sanas Virtual Audio Speaker - Select your connected headset Ringer - Select your connected headset Click Save Audio configuration - Custom profile Ensure your created profile is selected. pages.title: Cisco Jabber: Configure Audio Device
pages.text: summary Prev Next Introduction This guide provides step-by-step instructions for audio configuration on Cisco Jabber. Sanas requires continuous access to the audio stream to cancel noise from your audio in real time; therefore, Sanas devices must be selected under Cisco Jabber's audio settings. Sanas devices The following Sanas devices are available based on your operating system: Audio sources Window macOS Microphone Sanas Audio Sanas Microphone Speaker Sanas Audio Sanas Speaker Before you begin Ensure that Cisco Jabber and the Sanas applications are already installed on your computer. Ensure your Sanas App is running and activated. Ensure you have the required permissions on Jabber to modify the audio settings. Audio configuration 1. Launch Cisco Jabber Open the Cisco Jabber application. Log in with your credentials if prompted. 2. Access Audio Settings Click the Settings icon (gear icon) in the Jabber window. Navigate to File Options Select Audio from the left-side menu. 3. Select Sanas devices Select Sanas devices under the Microphone and Speaker drop-down menu. Note : Configure Sanas devices based on your Noise Cancellation setup: Inbound and Outbound Noise Cancellation — Select a Sanas device for both microphone and speaker. Outbound Noise Cancellation only — Select a Sanas device for microphone only. Adjust the audio level slider — we recommend a setting between 80% and 100% 4. Set audio device preferences On the Audio settings page, click Advanced at the bottom. In the Advanced audio options , set the device preference. Set the Sanas devices, as configured in step 3. 5. Save Changes Click Apply , then click OK to save your settings. Support Need help? Get in touch with our Support Team for assistance.

pages.title: Application Usage
pages.text: summary Prev Next FAQ Is there a usage limit since this is a free product? There is no usage limit. Free for all. Free forever Is there any latency in the audio when noise cancellation is used? The latency is ~40 milliseconds, and is imperceptible to the end users. If another human takes control of the microphone, will they be audible? Yes, the Sanas Noise Cancellation app just filters out background noise irrespective of the current speaker. Will the sounds from IVR system be cut out too? (such as Press 1 for X, Press 2 for Y…) The IVR system will remain unaffected. Noise cancellation only activates during the agent-customer interaction. If the enterprise is recording calls for training purposes, will noise be removed from these recordings? Yes, the background noises will be removed from all the call recordings because all recording happens downstream after the Sanas operations. Aside from cancelling background noise, does it change the quality or compression of a call? Sanas does not change call quality or apply any audio compression during the process. The audio’s incoming and outgoing bandwidth from the AI model remains the same. Does the software cancel background noise from the microphone and or the speaker? Can the agent hear the customers background noise and can the customer hear the agents background noise? Sanas cancels background noise from the agent’s microphone, meaning the agent can hear the customer clearly, but the customer won’t hear the agent’s background noise.

pages.title: Data Security & Privacy
pages.text: summary Prev Next Data Security & Privacy Do we record call data? Sanas does not record your calls. Our AI models process audio locally (on-device) without sending it to servers or cloud infrastructures. The application is designed to operate as a virtual microphone between your headset’s microphone and the recipient’s speaker. Hence, all of your calls are secure and remain unrecorded. Is Sanas compliant with any data security frameworks? At Sanas, we prioritize our customers’ data security above all. Our rigorous efforts to ensure data safety are reflected in our security portfolio. Sanas is compliant with the following data security frameworks: HIPAA SOC Type II GDPR ISO 27001 PCI DSS CCPA SOC Type III Visit our Trust Center page to look deeper at our implemented security controls. What is the purpose of each URL to be whitelisted? The URL whitelisting allows us to provide our services uninterruptedly. Below are the URLs and reasons behind whitelisting: *. sanas.ai – Required for app license activation and telemetry. *. document360.io – Provides access to our user guide (optional for whitelisting). https://cdn.auth0.com – Needed to download the application, as it is hosted on this CDN. What information is needed when setting up users? Do you need to use full names? You can sign up for Sanas Noise Cancellation for Free! You can add app users with basic user details like user IDs and full names.

pages.title: Troubleshooting & Support
pages.text: summary Prev Next FAQ Is there any risk of call disruption if the software malfunctions? Sanas has no dependency on call continuity. You can do the following to override Sanas’ Noise Cancellation during a call manually, if required: Disable Noise Cancellation from the App. Unselect Sanas Virtual Microphone from the softphone’s audio settings. What is the process for monitoring software vulnerabilities, who is responsible, and do they appear in the Sanas Portal? Every released feature and enhancement at Sanas undergoes rigorous internal testing by our QA team, ensuring the app remains optimized and works well for everyone. We manage our releases on the Sanas Portal; each includes a release note and version number for identification. Do you have auto app update functionality? How are updates or patches delivered—are they automated or customer-initiated? Yes, we provide an app auto-update feature, allowing a hassle-free app update and roll-outs. Is there customer support for the product? We have a dedicated Team that listens to and supports our customers. You can contact us at: Support@sanas.ai
